# About Us - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.644Z

## Content

New Student Services (NSS) empowers undergraduate students to succeed and facilitates their transition to UC Berkeley. This process is known as the Golden Bear Experience, which consists of two parts: Before Students Arrive (advising and prep, online) and After Students Arrive (Golden Bear Orientation, and Getting Your Bearings, on campus).
 
## Our Mission
 
The overarching goals of the Golden Bear Experience are to:
 
- welcome new students into UC Berkeley’s scholarly community and lay the foundation for fostering their intellectual identity 
- create opportunities for participants to gain an understanding of academic requirements 
- create opportunities for participants to connect with university and college resources, services, and support structures 
- create opportunities for participants to engage with campus traditions and the range of UC Berkeley’s unique cultural communities 
- create opportunities for participants to engage with their peers and the broader campus community 
- set the path for a lifelong relationship with the campus
 
The Golden Bear Experience for many years was fondly known as [Cal Student Orientation or CalSO](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/timewarp/history-of-calso/).
 
## Contact Us
 
**By mail:**
 New Student Services
 University of California, Berkeley
 Berkeley, California 94720
 
**By phone:** 510.642.7733
 
**By email:** [nss@berkeley.edu](mailto:nss@berkeley.edu)
 
To report spelling errors, outdated information, and/or incorrect or broken links on this website, please email us. Please note this website may link to other websites and technology applications. Our office does not monitor those websites or applications and has no technical or content control. Please contact the owners of those websites or applications for assistance.

# Accessing Your 1098-T Form Online Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/accessing-your-1098-t-form-online](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/accessing-your-1098-t-form-online)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.299Z

## Content

## Accessing Your 1098-T Form Online
 
By January 31, you should receive an email notification from UC Berkeley indicating your 1098-T form is available online via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx).
 
Please be sure to keep your email address on [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) current.
 
For Extension students, please visit the UC Berkeley Extension [SSN and ITIN FAQ(link is external)](https://extension.berkeley.edu/static/studentservices/ssn-faq/index.jsp) page.
 
Students may access their 1098-T form online via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx).
 
You will need the following information to login:
 
- Site ID (11554) 
- Username (Student ID) 
- Password (initial password is last 4 numbers of your SSN) 
- If you do not have an SSN, enter 0000 for the temporary password
 
If you have any difficulty logging in to the TAB Services website, please contact TAB Services toll free directly at (888) 220-2540.
 
Once you have logged in successfully, select the tax year from the drop-down menu box. You may search for your 1098-T form for the current tax year as well as the previous two tax years. After you have retrieved your 1098-T form online, you may print your form to be used with your tax preparation and filing.
      [## Access 1098-T forms via the TAB Services website
   (link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx)

# Alvin Tang - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/v-jara](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/v-jara)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.649Z

## Content

[![Alvin Tang](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Alvin.png)](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/a-tang/) 
Graduate Intern | [alqtang@berkeley.edu](mailto:alqtang@berkeley.edu)
 
Alvin joined the New Student Services as the Orientation Graduate Assistant in August 2024! He majored in Economics and specialized in Data Analytics and Economic Analysis at the University of California, Davis. He grew up in Oakland, CA, and has returned to the Bay Area to pursue his Master’s in Higher Education and Student Affairs from the University of San Francisco. As an undergraduate, his involvement in orientation motivated him to explore student life, and served in the inaugural cabinet of student leaders for the Vice Chancellor of Student Affairs. Additionally, he brings experience from university extension programs, K-12 non-profits, and commercial banking. In his spare time, he can be found trying new foods, swimming, volleyball, or video games.

[![Annah smiling sitting on a bench](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Annah.png)](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/student-leaders/student-coordinators/annah-brice/) 
Annah Brice (ɑnə bɹa͡ɪs) (she/her) is a transfer student in her fourth year and a Linguistics major. She was a Golden Bear Orientation Leader in Fall 2025 before joining the Student Coordinator team for Fall 2025. She worked as a Peer Advisor with the Re-Entry Student Program, where she supported nontraditional and transfer students in their transition to Berkeley. She applied to be a Student Coordinator to help foster a welcoming and empowering experience for incoming students while continuing to build community across campus. In her free time, Annah enjoys creative writing, cooking, and playing video games.

- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.643Z

## Content

## Become an Orientation Leader
 
As a Golden Bear Orientation Leader, you become part of a team that works collaboratively to welcome and orient new students to the UC Berkeley community. Using your own experiences and perspectives, you will help guide incoming students through a multi-day program in August, helping them explore academic life, campus involvement, and everything that UC Berkeley has to offer. This is a unique volunteer opportunity to:
 
- meet and mentor a diverse, dynamic student group 
- develop leadership skills 
- be a positive influence while having fun
 
![An Orientation Leader holding up a guidepost with the number 433, decorated to look like a rubber duck](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/group433-300x200.png)
 
## How to Join
 
The GBO Leader Application for 2026 is closed.
 
## Benefits for You
 
There are so many benefits to becoming a GBO Leader. Here are just a few:
 
- Leadership and professional development 
- Building your skills as a mentor 
- Extending your “Berkeley family” and learning more about campus resources 
- Creating memories with the GBO community 
- Exploring the Bay Area with new students 
- Getting UC Berkeley gear
 
![Two Orientation Leaders holding a guidepost labelled with the number 324, decorated with a teddy bear sitting on clouds](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/group324-300x200.png)
 
## Important Dates
 
In-person activities and expectations of all GBO Leaders:
 
- 1:1 Supervisor Check-In: April 2026 
- OL Spring Training: April 25, 2026 
- 2:1 Supervisor & OL Pair Check-in: July 2026 
- August Intensive Training: August 15-17, 2026 (full days) 
- Golden Bear Orientation: August 20-24, 2026 (full days)
 
## Role Description
 
- Serve as a positive and reliable role model for new students. 
- Participate fully in all required in-person events for GBO 2026, including 1:1 meetings, Orientation Leader training, and GBO programs. 
- Collaborate with an OL pair to orient and help create a welcoming and engaging GBO experience. *Pairs will be determined through* *a mutual selection process.* 
- Facilitate discussions related to Bear Foundations (diversity & inclusion), Bear Pact (sexual violence prevention and mental health), and other small-group activities. 
- Create an inclusive and welcoming community for all new students. 
- Encourage and support full participation for new students in GBO programming. 
- Guide new students to key campus locations and program points throughout GBO. 
- Respond to fundamental questions about UC Berkeley. 
- Collaborate effectively with a diverse range of people and work styles, while also being able to work independently. 
- Arrive on time, prepared, and ready to learn. 
- Demonstrate a willingness to grow both personally and professionally.
   

    
- Information Sessions & Eventsadd
Information Sessions:
 
- Orientation Leader Info Session #1 
- Thursday, February 19th at 4 pm | Location: 2610 Channing Way, 3rd Floor 
- Orientation Leader Info Session #2 
- Monday, March 9th at 6 pm | Location: [Online via Zoom](https://berkeley.zoom.us/j/97155822293)
 
Orientation Leader Recruitment Mixers:
 
- Thursday, January 29th at 5:30 pm | Location: Re-Entry Student Program (B North in the Martin Luther King Jr. Student Union Building) 
- Thursday, February 26th at 5:00 pm | Location: Stiles Hall Programming Space 
- Thursday, March 19th at 5:00 pm | Location: Unit 3 APR
- Qualificationsadd

 
- Be currently enrolled as an undergraduate student at UC Berkeley. 
- *If you graduate before GBO (i.e. spring or summer 2026), you can still participate as an OL as long as you commit to completing all required responsibilities.*
 
- - Possess a desire to support student transition. 
- Demonstrate leadership qualities. 
- Enjoy interacting with new students, families, faculty, and staff. 
- Have a passion and motivation to represent UC Berkeley and our community. 
- Be in good academic standing (hold a minimum 2.3 cumulative GPA). 
- *We encourage applicants to explain any exceptions to this guideline on the OL application form.*
 
- *Students who have Pass/No Pass grades from the past three semesters may still apply.*
 
- Extracurricular activities, internships, and employment may not conflict with OL required dates in the Spring or during August Training and Golden Bear Orientation (see above for exact dates). 
- *Resident Assistant (RA) positions may not be held due to schedule conflicts.*
- For Students Who Are Eligible for a Pell Grant or Dream Act Awardadd
If you are a student who is eligible for the Pell Grant or California Dream Act and you become a GBO Leader, then you are eligible for a $500 grant award.
 
In order to receive the grant, you must be a GBO Leader and complete all leader requirements. This award is to ensure that all students, no matter of financial situation, are able to volunteer as Orientation Leaders. Please reach out if you have questions or concerns regarding this opportunity: [nss@berkeley.edu](mailto:nss@berkeley.edu)

Charges on your student account may include registration fees, campus housing and telephone, University Health Services, and other miscellaneous debts. The charges may be due this month or in the future. For example, residence hall contract charges are assessed at the beginning of the semester and are due in five monthly payments.
 
Billing statements are produced monthly and are presented online. Please [log in to CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) for the most recent information about your student account including new charges, adjustments, aid disbursements, and payments.
 
Some or all instruction for all or part of the Academic Year may be delivered remotely. Tuition and fees have been set regardless of the method of instruction and will not be refunded in the event instruction occurs remotely for any part of the Academic Year. Figures for tuition and fees represent currently approved or proposed amounts and may not be final. Actual tuition and fees are subject to change by the University of California as determined to be necessary or appropriate. Final approved tuition and fee levels may differ from the amounts presented.

## Content

UC Berkeley students and delegates are encouraged to log into [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) to submit payments electronically. You may make payments online via ACH, credit card, electronic 529 plan withdrawals, and international funds transfers. Alternatively, checks and money orders are also accepted.
      
## Pay via Check (personal and 529 savings plans)
 
- Payments by check or money order must be issued in U.S. dollars drawn on a U.S. bank 
- Make checks payable to UC Regents 
- Reference your Student ID or UC Berkeley ID number on the memo line of the check
 
### Mail Checks To
 
University of California, Berkeley
Billing and Payment Services
PO Box 744884
Los Angeles, CA 90074-4884
 
#### Overnight Courier Delivery
 
For overnight or express delivery checks please mail to the following address:
 
Bank of America Lockbox Services
Lockbox 744884
2706 Media Center Drive
Los Angeles, CA 90065-1733
 
### Drop Box Location
 
Our drop box is located at 2610 Channing Way, Berkeley, CA 94720, outside and to the right of the main entrance.
 
## Outside Agency Scholarships
 
Scholarship checks require special processing to ensure awards are recorded properly.
 
Please refer to the [Managing Outside Scholarship Awards(link is external)](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/types-of-aid-at-berkeley/scholarships/outside-scholarships/) page for specific instructions on where to mail your scholarship check.

# Delinquent Accounts Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/billing/delinquent-accounts](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/billing/delinquent-accounts)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.295Z

## Content

You are responsible for monitoring charges on your student account and ensuring that payments are made in a timely manner. Please note that charges on your student account may have different due dates. Do not assume all charges are due at the same time.
 
To view new charges and the most recent information on your account, please refer to the 'My Finances' page in [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
 
If your account becomes delinquent, a block may be placed on your student account that can affect registration in future terms.
 
Additionally, students who are no longer enrolled in the university and who have a past due balance may face additional collection action including placement with the California Franchise Tax Board and with collection agencies. Student accounts placed with a collection agency may be reported to one or more credit bureaus without further notification. Once referred to a collection agency, you will be referred to that agency for payment arrangements.
 
Payments made to your student account will apply to the oldest charges first. If you have past due charges, payments will apply to these charges and will not be redirected to pay newer charges.
 
Please visit the Office of the Registrar website to learn how this relates to the [Cancel for Non-Payment Policy(link is external)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/registration/cancellation-withdrawal/cnp).

8f9fc6281b136bfb.title: Disability Accommodations - Golden Bear Orientation
8f9fc6281b136bfb.content:
# Disability Accommodations - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/disability-accommodations](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/disability-accommodations)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.642Z

## Content

UC Berkeley is committed to providing full access to all of our programs and services for our students with disabilities. If you require **accommodations for a disability**(visible or invisible) to fully participate in Golden Bear Orientation, please let us know.
 
In order to achieve the goals of Golden Bear Orientation including making connections, learning resources, engaging in community discussions, and developing community, participation in the program includes:
 
- listening to presentations 
- reading written materials and handouts 
- traveling across campus and city participating in small groups 
- engaging with large and small groups, including meal times
 
New Student Services works with the [Disabled Students’ Program (DSP)](http://dsp.berkeley.edu/students/new-students) and [Disability Access and Compliance](https://dac.berkeley.edu/home) to provide accommodations for the week of Golden Bear Orientation. You may receive communication from either or both offices as we work to address your accommodations request(s) at GBO and as you prepare for the upcoming academic year. Below is a list of potential accommodations. Please use this as a reference as you consider the support you will need to participate in GBO. The below list is not exhaustive, so please let us know if there’s anything else you require.
 
- physical/wheelchair access to locations 
- accessible public transportation 
- CART captioning for events and groups 
- closed captioning on videos 
- reading assistance/alternative media formats 
- live stream of events (those with outside small group activities, some late night events, meals and excursions)
 
Some groups may need to switch activities based on disability if we are able to host in person programs (example: hiking). Please submit your request for accommodations by filling out the form below with as much advance notice as possible. In general, the more notice we receive of an accommodation request, the better prepared we can be to address it. We will always give a good faith effort to complete late requests.
 
## Submit Your Request
 
If you require accommodations for a disability (visible or invisible) to fully participate in GBO, please submit your request by [**completing this online form**](https://forms.gle/xEq35hfyYUv9S1kYA). Please make sure to access the form using you Berkeley email address. We appreciate as much advance notice as possible to better prepare to address your needs. The form also collects information for full exemptions to GBO participation. For information about participation expectations, please review our [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|Policies page]].
 

 
## Sensory Experience
 
You may have questions about what Golden Bear Orientation is really like. New Student Services has created a GBO Sensory Guide that summarizes all events, including locations, sites, sounds, audience size, etc. Review the [GBO Fall 2026 NSS Sensory Guide.](https://canva.link/srpxrzc2oz71hco)

d9cb723196baf84b.path: Editing the Dollar Amount of an Online Payment Student Billing.md
d9cb723196baf84b.content:
# Editing the Dollar Amount of an Online Payment Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/payments-and-refunds/online-payments/editing-dollar-amount-online-payment](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/payments-and-refunds/online-payments/editing-dollar-amount-online-payment)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Instructions
 
### 1. [Log In to CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu)
 
- [https://calcentral.berkeley.edu(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu)
 
### 2. Click the 'My Finances' menu tab
 
- From the CalCentral home page, click the 'My Finances' menu tab
 
### 3. Click the 'Make Payment' button
 
- Navigate to the 'Billing Summary' section on the 'My Finances' page and click the 'Make Payment' button 
- After clicking the 'Make Payment' button, a new window will open and you will be signed in to the Transact portal
      ![Screenshot of the CalCentral My Finances page with Make Payment button](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/calcentral_my_finances_page_with_make_payment_button.jpg?itok=URifnVr9&timestamp=1606254773)      
### 4. Click the 'Make a payment' button
 
- From the Transact 'Overview' page, click the 'Make a payment' button to initiate the transaction
      ![Screenshot of the CashNet Overview page with Balance summary](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/cashnet_overview_page_balance_summary.jpg?itok=I7zT3jqu&timestamp=1615243018)      
### 5. Click in the 'Amount' box to edit the payment amount
 
- How much would you like to pay? 
- From the 'Pay Amount' page, enter the amount you wish to pay 
- Your current Balance amount should automatically be entered in the 'Amount' box 
- To pay less than the Balance amount, click in the 'Amount' box to edit the payment amount 
- Do not pay more than the Balance amount due 
- The Balance amount reflects up-to-date activity on your account 
- Payments are applied to charges in order of due date, beginning with the oldest date first
      ![Screenshot of the CashNet Make a Payment page with Pay Amount option](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/cashnet_make_a_payment_page_pay_amount.jpg?itok=IvJ5mN_8&timestamp=1615504265)      
### 6. Click the 'Continue' button after entering the amount you wish to pay
      ![Screenshot of the CashNet Continue button](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/cashnet_continue_button.jpg?itok=uKTBIIm3&timestamp=1615242642)      
### 7. Select a payment method and click the 'Continue' button
 
- How would you like to pay? 
- From the 'Payment Method' page, select a payment method you wish to use and click the 'Continue' button 
- Payment method options are: 
- Credit or Debit Card 
- A non-refundable service fee applies to credit card payments: 
- 2.95% for domestic card payments 
- 4.25% for international card payments 
- The minimum service fee for card transactions over $20 and less than $102 will be $3 
- Bank Account 
- Electronic checks (ACH) that are returned by your bank for any reason are subject to a non-refundable Returned Payment Fee of $25 
- 529 Savings Plan 
- A $10.00 non-refundable convenience fee will apply to electronic 529 payments 
- [[International Payments Student Billing|International Payment]]
      ![Screenshot of the CashNet Make a Payment page with Payment Method options](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/cashnet_make_a_payment_page_payment_method.jpg?itok=dmjfrTq-&timestamp=1689113949)      ![Screenshot of the CashNet Continue button](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/cashnet_continue_button.jpg?itok=uKTBIIm3&timestamp=1615242642)      
### 8. Enter the required information for the payment method selected
 
- Credit or Debit Card 
- 529 Savings Plan 
- [[International Payments Student Billing|International Payment]] 
- [[International Payments via Flywire Student Billing|International Payments via Flywire]] 
- [[International Payments via Convera Student Billing|International Payments via Convera]]
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)

7a5c48a9b33d77d6.title: FAQS - Golden Bear Orientation
7a5c48a9b33d77d6.content:
# FAQS - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/faqs](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/faqs)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.642Z

## Content

*Updated March 16, 2026*
 
## Q: Is Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) in person?
 
A: Yes- Fall 2026 GBO will be done in a fully in person format. There may be limited virtual access to programming such as recordings of events, but there is no overall virtual orientation experience. Those who are unable to attend orientation in-person or have extenuating circumstances are encouraged to check out our [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|Policies]] page of our website and fill out the [Golden Bear Orientation Fall 2026: Exemption and Accommodations](https://forms.gle/xEq35hfyYUv9S1kYA) form by Sunday, July, 19, 2026. You can reference the emails from New Student Services for details and the GBO Sample Schedule page for updated schedules.
 
## Q: I have unique circumstances that may limit how I am able to engage in GBO programs and/or other experiences. What can NSS do?
 
A: If you believe you will not be able to engage with GBO or may need unique accommodations to participate in the program due to your circumstances, reach out to New Student Services as soon as possible. More information about this process can be found on the [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|Policies]] page of our website.
 
## Q: Is there a cost associated with Golden Bear Orientation?
 
A: Yes, all new students are required to pay the New Student Programming Fee. You will be assessed a fee on your first semester CalCentral bill. The New Student Programming Fee is $550 for incoming Fall 2026 undergraduates ($370 for UCEAP students). If applicable, look at your financial aid package to see if this fee will be covered by financial aid in the form of the “New Student Grant.” If you have financial concerns related to the New Student Programming Fee, please complete the [Golden Bear Orientation Fall 2026: Exemption and Accommodations Form](https://forms.gle/xEq35hfyYUv9S1kYA) (Those who receive a full exemption will have the New Student Programming Fee removed). Please refer to our Office of the [Registrar Tuition & Fees](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/tuition-fees-residency/tuition-fees) page for more details on student fees.
 
These are the [[Dates & Deadlines - Golden Bear Orientation|critical dates for the Golden Bear Experience]], including Golden Bear Orientation (GBO). This page is updated often so please refresh your web browser each time you visit.
 
## Q: I am a UCEAP student studying abroad at Berkeley. Do I have to participate in the Golden Bear Experience, including attending Golden Bear Orientation?
 
A: UCEAP students are no longer required to attend Golden Bear Orientation (GBO), but are invited to opt into participation in the five day, in person GBO August 19-24, 2026. This change was made to reflect the unique needs of UCEAP students studying at Berkeley.
 
UCEAP students can opt into attending Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) in person by completing the [Fall 2026 UCEAP GBO Opt-In Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSe8aT5pYhkP5iA22GBmeVgPC5k3ZaTaAwIvng5ywcb9GPhBxA/viewform) by the deadline of **July 19, 2026.** Note that this form requires you to be logged into your UC Berkeley email account (bMail). Submission of the Fall 2026 UCEAP GBO Opt-In Form will provide full access to the five day program and require payment of the EAP New Student Programming Fee of $370.
 
Requests to opt into the program after July 19, 2026 will be reviewed on a case by case basis and will require participants to pay the EAP New Student Programming Fee of $370.
 
UCEAP students will still receive [[Golden Bear Prep - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Prep International]], an online module meant to introduce students to life outside the classroom prior to arriving on campus and must attend the required [Virtual EAP Orientation with Berkeley International Office (BIO)](https://internationaloffice.berkeley.edu/students/exchange) on Wednesday, August 19, 2026 whether or not they choose to opt into GBO in person.
 
Questions? Reach out to New Student Services via email ([nss@berkeley.edu](mailto:nss@berkeley.edu)) and our team will help your transition to UC Berkeley.
 
## Q: What meals will be provided during GBO?
 
A: During your participation in Golden Bear Orientation (GBO), you will experience a variety of dining options. You will have the opportunity to experience our various Berkeley Dining facilities in the residence halls, have one meal at a local restaurant on Telegraph Avenue, and frequent a fleet of food trucks while picnicking at the Campanile. All of these venues will be on your schedule at some point, regardless of your status as residential or off-campus student. Due to the limited capacity of the various dining options, you will have scheduled meal times and will be escorted to these various locations by your Orientation Leader. This meticulous coordination across all the options ensures that we minimize wait times while also accommodating your other programmatic obligations throughout the day. Furthermore, most dining platforms can accommodate the following dietary restrictions: gluten-free*, Halal, Kosher**, vegan, and vegetarian.**If you have severe food allergies or dietary restrictions beyond what has been mentioned, you are highly encouraged to submit the**[**Exemptions and Accommodations Form**](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc82pEYl3PSlVoyZqmrRgwgONB3JN2oiwkHC8bRx8niUwESPQ/viewform?usp=header)**and we may reach out to you to learn more about how we can best help you navigate our program. For a more detailed list of dining options, please see a**[[GBO Sample Schedule - Golden Bear Orientation|**Sample Schedule**]]**.**
 
**Gluten free meals at Bite of Berkeley restaurants and food trucks may not be fully accessible to those with severe wheat allergies/Celiacs. Berkeley Dining facilities do have allergen friendly stations where these needs can be met. Please complete the Exemptions and Accommodations Form to help us better understand your needs.*
 
***Certified Kosher meals can be made available at Berkeley Dining platforms with advance notice. Food trucks and Bite of Berkeley meals may not have selections that meet your needs depending on your level or Kosher practice. If you follow a Kosher diet, please provide more information in our form and we will follow up with you individually to provide more details. Please complete the Exemptions and Accommodations Form to help us better understand your needs.*
 
## Q: How will I find community as a new student?
 
A: We know that building community is essential to success at Berkeley and new students’ first couple semesters are extremely important for building their community. In addition to offering a fun array of community-building activities as part of GBO, we are actively exploring different ways to help connect students with their peers and engage with their co-curricular interests. Visit Student Affairs’ [Berkeley Life blog](https://life.berkeley.edu/) for ideas on how to find community.
 
## Q: How will I be connected to current UC Berkeley students? How will I be connected to other new students?
 
A: During GBO, we plan to have multiple opportunities for you to learn from the experiences of current UC Berkeley students. A key component of GBO is the small group experience led by Orientation Leaders (OLs). OLs are continuing students who are volunteering their time to help make your transition to Berkeley smooth. They will guide you and a small group of fellow incoming students through programs during GBO. Your small group will consist of other incoming students, either first years or transfers depending on your incoming status.
 
## Q: I don’t know where I am living this fall/spring, what does that mean for me and GBO?
 
A: Regardless of where you choose to live, New Student Services is committed to facilitating your transition to UC Berkeley. GBO programming is not based solely on where you chose to live and/or if you live in University Residence Halls. Incoming students will have the ability to connect with their small group, as well as other communities (academic, identity, interest, etc.).
 
## Q: I have questions about housing, course enrollment, financial aid, etc. Who do I talk to and how?
 
A: While our Office Representatives are more than happy to connect you with other campus resources, unfortunately they are not able to answer certain questions that fall out of our office’s function. Here is a list of other departments that may provide a more direct answer for your questions:
 
- For questions related to financial aid, fees and tuition, billing, payments, and disbursements, registration and enrollment, and student records, contact [Cal Student Central](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/services-areas-support/). 
- For questions regarding registration, transferring credits, transcripts, residency requirements, veterans benefits, and other related issues, contact the [Office of the Registrar](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/about/contact-us/). 
- For questions about issues that relate to your Conditions of Admission (I.e., sending in transcripts/exam scores by a certain deadline, status updates on receiving student records), contact the [Office of Undergraduate Admissions](https://admissions.berkeley.edu/contact-us) 
- For questions related to housing (move-in, contracts, deadlines, offers, etc.), please contact [UC Berkeley Housing](https://housing.berkeley.edu/contact-us/).
 
## Q: I am sick or unable to attend GBO due to unexpected circumstances. What does this mean for me and GBO?
 
If you get sick or are dealing with an unexpected situation, please take care of yourself appropriately and reach out to us. You should not come to in-person activities if you are sick. Please email the New Student Services team, and we will work with you individually to determine possible solutions. We recognize that, if there are barriers to your participation in GBO, these barriers will likely impact your entire Berkeley experience.
 
You are always welcome to contact our office at (510) 642-7733 or through email at nss@berkeley.edu if you may be unsure about which office would be appropriate to contact for your concerns.
 
For any specific questions you have, feel free to email nss@berkeley.edu. Our NSS Representatives will be happy to refer you to the right resources based on your needs! While we may not be the main point of contact, we focus on helping students connect with resources that they will utilize throughout their entire Berkeley career.

5bcfb029747bcf20.content:
# Faculty & Staff FAQs for Fall Start - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/how-to-get-involved/staff-faculty-volunteer-opportunities/faculty-staff-faqs-for-fall-start](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/how-to-get-involved/staff-faculty-volunteer-opportunities/faculty-staff-faqs-for-fall-start)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.644Z

## Content

We understand that Golden Bear Orientation, Move-In Day, and the start of the fall semester has an impact on our campus, including faculty and staff. We also need your support in creating a welcoming and supportive environment on our campus for our new students! Here are answers to questions about what we are doing to welcome new students, how it will affect our campus, and ways the Berkeley community can contribute.
 
If you have a question that is not addressed here, please email New Student Services: [nss@berkeley.edu](mailto:nss@berkeley.edu)
 
## What are new students doing at the start of the semester?
 
Undergraduate first year and transfer students have a lot to accomplish at the beginning of the semester. They Move-In to campus housing the week of **August 17, 2026** and directly following they participate in Golden Bear Orientation and Getting Your Bearings (in-person programs that help orient them once they are on campus). For key dates, see our [[Dates & Deadlines - Golden Bear Orientation|Dates & Deadlines]] page.
 
## How will I be affected as a member of the Berkeley community and how can I prepare?
 
The biggest impact to staff and faculty will be on Move-In Day and also during Golden Bear Orientation. For the current dates, see our [[Dates & Deadlines - Golden Bear Orientation|Dates & Deadlines]] page.
 
We have 9,000+ new students who will be transitioning to campus during those times!
 
About 8,000 new undergraduates will be moving in the week of August 17, 2026, many accompanied by family and others supporting them.
 
During Golden Bear Orientation, you’ll see groups of new students, led by Student Coordinators, participating in various orientation activities.
 
All of these activities may lead to more crowds and lines than normal. However, we still encourage you to be present on campus to provide a welcoming and bustling environment for our students. Here are some suggestions for how to beat the crowds:
 
- Stay up-to-date with your bMail, where we will send updates regarding road closures and parking updates 
- Bring your lunch that week so you don’t have to wait in long restaurant lines 
- Give yourself a little extra time to get to meetings or appointments on campus 
- Avoid scheduling vendor meetings or inviting outside guests to campus during orientation week
 
## How can I support the new students?
 
If you are a faculty or staff member, we have many ways for you to be more formally involved. Learn about [[Staff & Faculty Volunteer Opportunities - Golden Bear Orientation|staff and faculty volunteer opportunities]]. If you believe your department should be more closely involved with the program, please email New Student Services at: [nss@berkeley.edu](mailto:nss@berkeley.edu).
 
## Where do I direct key student questions?
 
Students may have a lot of questions as they come to campus. Here are some of the most common questions and some resources to point students to:
 
### Housing move-in and parking
 
See our [housing move-in](http://housing.berkeley.edu/living-on-campus/move-in/) page.
 
### Additional housing questions
 
Including questions about assignments, roommates, and more. See [housing faqs by audience type](http://housing.berkeley.edu/resources/faqs/).
 
### Golden Bear Orientation
 
Including check-in, schedule, and more. During GBO, New Student Services staffs a GBO Help Desk on Upper Sproul Plaza from 8:00am-6:00pm Thursday, August 20-Monday, August 24. See the [[Golden Bear Orientation Overview - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Orientation overview]] for additional questions.
 
### Getting a Cal 1 Card (the Berkeley ID card)
 
Find instructions for new students on [how to get a Cal 1 Card](http://cal1card.berkeley.edu/get-a-card/new-students).
 
### Financial aid, registration, billing, enrollment, payments
 
Get help through [Cal Student Central](http://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/services-areas-support/) virtually, in-person, or through an online chatbot.
 
### Meal plans and dining locations
 
Browse the dining website which has information on [meal plans](http://dining.berkeley.edu/meal-plans/2024-2025/) and [dining locations and hours of operation](http://dining.berkeley.edu/locations/).

d24109466814aa7c.content:
# Federal Perkins and Institutional Loan Repayment Information Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/federal-perkins-and-institutional-loan-repayment-information](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/federal-perkins-and-institutional-loan-repayment-information)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.298Z

## Content

## Overview
 
The University of California has engaged the services of Heartland ECSI, Inc. as the servicer for all of the university's Federal Perkins and Institutional loans including, but not limited to, sending student loan billing statements, processing student loan payments, forbearance, deferment, and cancellation request forms, and providing quality customer service to our student loan borrowers. Heartland ECSI does not service Federal Direct Loans.
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Registering with Heartland ECSI
 
Heartland ECSI, requires student loan borrowers to register on their website and create a profile. Please use the following instructions to register and access your account information, take advantage of expanded payment options, and to sign up for electronic statements:
 
### Step 1: ECSI Website
 
Navigate to the [Heartland ECSI(link is external)](https://heartland.ecsi.net) website.
 
### Step 2: Register and Create a Profile
 
From the ECSI home page, click the 'Register' link and create a profile.
 
### Step 3: Connect Your Account
 
Connect your account using your Heartland Key visible on your billing statement.
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Tips to Managing Repayment
 
Keep a paper file just for your student loan materials and keep a folder on your laptop just for your student loan information too. This provides easy reference for yourself.
 
If you have a Federal Direct Loan, it will be serviced elsewhere and can be viewed by logging in to Federal Student Aid from their [Manage Loans(link is external)](https://studentaid.gov/h/manage-loans) page. If you have a private student loan from a third party, please go to the third party website to manage those loans.
 
Most loans have deferment or forbearance options. If you are having trouble making payments, it is better to reach out to your loan servicer than risk default.
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Know Your Student Loan Repayment Obligation
 
A student loan is a serious and important financial obligation, and you must repay your loan.
 
You are required to repay your loan(s) regardless of whether you complete your education, are able to find employment, or are satisfied with your education.
Repayment is required according to the terms of your promissory note.
 
You must provide your loan servicer with corrections to your name, address, references, Social Security number, and driver's license information.
 
You may be able to apply for deferment, forbearance, or cancellation of your loan payments. (Refer to your promissory note.)
 
If you do not apply for deferment or cancellation, you must pay your loan(s) as scheduled.
 
You can prepay all or part of your loan(s) at any time without penalty.
 
You may be eligible to defer repayment if you go to another institution of higher education. Contact ECSI Customer Service Advocate via Live Chat from the [Heartland ECSI(link is external)](https://heartland.ecsi.net) website, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 8:00 PM EST, or toll-free phone at 888-549-3274, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 9:00 PM EST.
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Apply For Loan Deferment, Cancellation, or Consolidation (If Necessary)
 
### Deferment
 
Deferment is a period of time during repayment in which the borrower, upon meeting certain conditions, is not required to make payments of loan principal and sometimes interest. Deferment of your Perkins or Institutional loan may be granted if:
 
- You are enrolled at least half time at an accredited institution 
- You are a member of the armed forces or various public or private volunteer organizations (e.g., Peace Corps or VISTA) 
- You are in advanced professional training
 
Get deferment forms for Perkins borrowers at the [Heartland ECSI(link is external)](https://heartland.ecsi.net/) website.
 
### Cancellation
 
Cancellation of your obligation to repay your Perkins loan may be granted if you are employed in:
 
- Teaching 
- Early intervention services 
- Law enforcement or corrections 
- Nursing or medical technician position 
- Child or family services 
- Head Start 
- Military
 
All loans can be discharged for total and permanent disability and death.
 
### Consolidation
 
Consolidation combines all of your federal loans into one loan:
 
- You must be in your repayment period to apply for consolidation 
- Your interest rate will be fixed for the length of the loan 
- You may include your Perkins loan, but once consolidated, you are no longer eligible for the cancellation options listed on your Perkins promissory note 
- Under consolidation, interest will accrue similar to an unsubsidized loan
 
Consolidation information for all borrowers is available at the Federal Student Aid's [Direct Consolidation Loan Application(link is external)](https://studentaid.gov/loan-consolidation/) web page.
 
For more specific information, read your promissory note(s), or contact your loan servicer.
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Repay Your Student Loan(s)
 
If you cannot meet the repayment schedule on your university-based student loan(s), contact the Student Loan Coordinator at [accountconsultants@berkeley.edu(link sends e-mail)](mailto:accountconsultants@berkeley.edu).
 
### If You Are Delinquent on Your Student Loan(s)
 
Please be aware of the following if you are delinquent on your student loan(s):
 
- You may have to pay late fees, collection costs, and/or interest in addition to the loan amount 
- Your credit rating may be adversely affected 
- Your state income tax refund could be withheld 
- You may be ineligible for further student aid, deferments, forbearances, and loan consolidation 
- Additionally, it could impact your ability to future enrollment

7510addfd8eb9cb5.content:
# Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/fpp](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/fpp)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Overview
 
- The Fee Payment Plan (FPP) allows for qualified registration fees to be paid in five monthly installments 
- For current registration fee amounts, please see the Tuition and Fees page on the Office of the Registrar web site 
- The FPP enrollment is established on a per semester basis, not an academic year 
- When you enroll in the FPP, you will be required to pay a non-refundable participation fee of $60 (this fee is subject to change per semester) 
- The non-refundable FPP participation fee will be due with the first installment 
- Please refer to the [[Frequently Asked Questions - Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing|Fee Payment Plan FAQ]] web page if you have further questions
      ![Decorative line](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/line-berkeley_blue_dark_3840x10.png?itok=ZaEE5pH4&timestamp=1688082258)      
## Eligibility
 
### Fees and Programs Eligible for the Fee Payment Plan
 
- Undergraduate and Graduate Fall and Spring Semester Fees 
- Tuition 
- Non-resident Supplemental Tuition 
- Berkeley Campus Fee 
- Student Services Fee 
- Transit Fee 
- All Graduate level Program Fees 
- Professional Degree Supplemental Tuition 
- Course Materials Fees 
- Law Instructional Materials Fee 
- UC Extension Fall Program for Freshmen 
- Graduate Self Supporting Degree Program Summer Semester Fees 
- Instructional Resilience and Enhancement Fee (IREF)
 
### Fees and Programs Not Eligible for the Fee Payment Plan
 
- Student Programming and Orientation Fee 
- Health Insurance Fee 
- Document Management Fee 
- Drop/Add Fees 
- Filing Fee

- Concurrent Enrollment

## Enrollment
 
### How to Enroll in the FPP
 
- Log into Cal Central 
- Click on the 'My Finances' tab 
- Navigate to 'Tuition and Fee Payment Plan (FPP)' in the 'Financial Resources' section 
- Click on 'Activate Plan' 
- Review the Installments 
- Complete the Agreement 
- Review and Save the Installment Schedule 
- Submit your first payment
 
Please note: The FPP enrollment is established on a per semester basis, not on an academic year. Additionally, fees must be assessed (min. balance of $600) before you can enroll in the FPP.
 
### Deadline to Enroll in the FPP
 
#### Fall Term
 
- September (please refer to the second installment due date)
 
#### Spring Term
 
- February (please refer to the second installment due date)
 
#### Summer Term
 
- Self Supporting Degree Programs only

# Frequently Asked Questions - Charges and Fees Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/charges-and-fees](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/charges-and-fees)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Charges and Fees
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will students pay for access?]]
   
The access charge for Inclusive Access materials will be added to your student billing account after the drop/add deadline, which is around the 5th week of the semester. The charge will appear as Bookstore – Inclusive Access. Students who opt out by the posted deadline for the current term will not be billed.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I'm no longer an active student. How can I view my student account?]]
   
For information on how to view your account, please review the [Alumni and Non-Current Student(link is external)](https://sis.berkeley.edu/alumni-and-non-current-students) job aid.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will my fees be different depending on the mode of instruction?]]
   
Some or all instruction for all or part of the Academic Year may be delivered remotely. Tuition and mandatory fees have been set regardless of the method of instruction and will not be refunded in the event instruction occurs remotely for any part of the Academic Year. Figures for tuition and fees represent currently approved amounts and may not be final. Actual tuition and fees are subject to change by the University of California as determined to be necessary or appropriate. Final approved tuition and fee levels may differ from the amounts presented.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|When will I receive my Fall or Spring bill?]]
   
Fall Charges:
 
- We will post the charges to your account around mid July provided that you have enrolled in units. When the charges have been posted to your account you will receive an email notification. At that time you will see the balance due on your CalCentral student portal and remit payment.
 
Spring Charges:
 
- We will post the charges to your account around mid November provided that you have enrolled in units. When the charges have been posted to your account you will receive an email notification. At that time you will see the balance due on your CalCentral student portal and remit payment.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will I be charged a fee to make a credit or debit card payment online?]]
   
Students and delegates can pay charges online using a credit or debit card. A non-refundable service fee applies to all card payments. The fee is 2.95% for domestic card payments and 4.25% for international card payments. The minimum service fee for card transactions over $20 and less than $102 will be $3. To make a credit or debit card payment, log in to [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/), select the 'My Finances' tab and click the 'Make Payment' button.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|The charges on my account were paid at the beginning of the semester with financial aid or with personal payment. Why am I receiving a statement now?]]
   
There are several reasons why new charges may appear on your account. If you have questions regarding charges appearing on your account, please contact Cal Student Central. You can visit [Cal Student Central(link is external)](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/) to open a case, locate operating hours, or you can contact a counselor by calling 510 664 9181.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why is there a "Telecom" charge on my account?]]
   
The campus provides students who live in residence halls, Manville and International House, with access to a land telephone line. The basic charge for this line is required in the terms and conditions of your housing contract, whether or not the line is used. The fee is billed each semester.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why do I have a $10.00 CalPIRG fee on my account?]]
   
Students who voluntarily pledge to support CalPIRG (California Student Public Interest Research Group, Inc.) are billed this fee to their account. The fee is billed each semester until the student contacts CalPIRG to withdraw their support. Questions related to this fee should be referred to the CalPIRG office via email at [info@calpirgstudents.org(link sends e-mail)](mailto:info@calpirgstudents.org).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I am being billed for student health insurance. How can I waive out of it?]]
   
All students are billed for health insurance. Students wishing to waive out of health insurance must submit a waiver. Deadlines to submit your waiver can be found on the [UHS Waiving SHIP(link is external)](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/insurance-ship/waiving-ship) page. Questions related to this fee should be referred to the Student Health Insurance Office at 510 642 5700.

# Frequently Asked Questions - Check Payments Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/check-payments](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/check-payments)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Check Payments
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I make a payment by check?]]
   
A payment from a checking account can be made in the following ways:
 
- Electronically online through your CalCentral account 
- Checks can be sent through the mail 
- Please refer to the [[Check Payments Student Billing|Check Payments]] page for mailing instructions 
- Checks can be placed in the payment drop box located at the entrance of 2610 Channing Way, Berkeley, CA 94720
 
UC Berkeley does not operate cashiering windows for student account payments. Please make sure that the student's full name and ID number is indicated on the check.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I submit my payment at Sproul Hall?]]
   
Check payments can be submitted by mail (please refer to the [[Check Payments Student Billing|Check Payments]] page for mailing instructions) or can be placed in the payment drop box located at the entrance of 2610 Channing Way, Berkeley, CA 94720.
 
UC Berkeley does not operate cashiering windows for student account payments. Please make sure that the student's full name and ID number is indicated on the check.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|If I place my payment in the drop box, when will it post to my student account?]]
   
Check payments placed in the drop box located at the 2610 Channing Way, Berkeley, CA 94720 address will be processed weekly on Thursdays. During peak periods, payments will be processed 3 times a week on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
 
For faster processing, please submit payments online via [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will I be charged a fee to make an online payment from my checking account?]]
   
Students and delegates are not charged a fee to make an e-Check payment (ACH). To make an electronic payment, log in to [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/), select the 'My Finances' tab and click the 'Make Payment' button. You will need to know the bank routing number and bank account number to submit the payment. Please be sure to enter this information accurately.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will I be charged a fee if my check or electronic check (ACH) is returned unpaid by the bank?]]
   
Yes.
 
Checks and electronic checks (ACH) that are returned by your bank for any reason are subject to a Returned Payment Fee of $25. When entering bank account and routing information online, please verify the information you have entered to ensure the item is not returned by your bank. Please do not use your ATM/Debit cards numbers in lieu of your checking account number, as the payment will be rejected by your bank and a non refundable Returned Payment Fee of $25 will be assessed.

# Frequently Asked Questions - Direct Deposit Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/direct-deposit](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/direct-deposit)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Direct Deposit
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|If I enroll in Direct Deposit, does this give the university authorization to debit my account?]]
   
No. Enrolling in Direct Deposit only allows the university to directly deposit your refunds into your bank account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Which student payments are eligible for Direct Deposit?]]
   
- Refunds, graduate student stipends, and any non-payroll university payments to students (except Emergency Loan checks) can be directly deposited to your bank account 
- Some outside agency payments may be processed via direct deposit, while some may not 
- Student employees can have their paychecks deposited automatically to their bank account each payday. Please contact your hiring department for a special form and more information
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will the money be deposited to my bank account?]]
   
The money will be deposited electronically. Direct deposit is fast, convenient, safe, and reliable.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How soon will my direct deposit start?]]
   
After you submit your bank information, direct deposit will be activated within 7 business days. Once set up, refunds will continue to go to your designated bank account until you either cancel your authorization or edit your bank account information online.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will I know when the money has been sent to my bank?]]
   
You will be notified via e-mail one business day before each deposit is sent to the bank. Please check with your bank to verify the deposit of the funds into your account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Are there any reasons why the money would not be deposited to my bank?]]
   
If you close your bank account, the transfer will not automatically go to a new account. To avoid the disruption of direct deposits, you must update your bank account information through the Direct Deposit website 7 business days prior to closing your bank account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What else do I need to know?]]
   
- If you do not have direct deposit, a paper check will be mailed to your local address within 10 business days 
- Please make sure you review and update your local address information in [Cal Central(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) 
- You may cancel your direct deposit authorization at any time through the [Direct Deposit website(link is external)](https://eftstudent.berkeley.edu/) 
- All funds must be deposited to an account in your name 
- The bank you designate to receive your direct deposit must be in the United States 
- We cannot issue deposits to accounts held at investment firms 
- If you receive funds you are not entitled to, you will be billed for repayment

# Frequently Asked Questions - Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/fee-payment-plan-fpp](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/fee-payment-plan-fpp)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Fee Payment Plan (FPP)
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|I enrolled in the Fee Payment Plan last semester. Do I need to enroll in the plan each semester?]]
   
Yes. You must enroll in the Fee Payment Plan each fall and spring semester. The option to pay in installments is not available for Summer Session and for some programs. To learn more about this payment option, visit the [[Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing|Fee Payment Plan]] page.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can someone other than the student activate the Fee Payment Plan?]]
   
No.
 
Only a student can activate the Fee Payment Plan through [Cal Central(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). While a student may give a parent/other person delegate access to view financials and pay bills, only the student can activate the FPP.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Do I need to make a payment to activate the plan?]]
   
No.
 
After activating the Fee Payment Plan, you must pay an amount equal to the first installment by the Friday prior to term instruction to avoid cancellation. If a payment is made before the FPP is activated, the FPP will recalculate based on the new principal balance due, and the first installment payment will still be required.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I have partial financial aid and want to be on the Fee Payment Plan. Do I need to make a payment to activate the FPP?]]
   
No.
 
Payment will not be required to activate the Fee Payment Plan. Financial aid will reduce the balance, and the FPP will recalculate based on the new balance. The 5 payment installments will adjust accordingly.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I mail in my payment. Can someone at UC Berkeley activate the Fee Payment Plan for me?]]
   
No.
 
In order to participate in the Fee Payment Plan, you must complete the process online.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What happens if I don’t pay my installment by the due date?]]
   
If you do not make payment according to the due dates outlined in your Installment Schedule, you may incur late fees and have a block placed on your account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is the Fee Payment Plan participation fee refundable?]]
   
No.
 
You will be charged a non-refundable $60 fee to participate in the Fee Payment Plan.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I set up the Fee Payment Plan for the whole academic year?]]
   
No.
 
You are not able to enroll in the FPP for the full academic year. You can only enroll in the Fee Payment Plan at the beginning of each term. Please visit the Enrollment section on the [[Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing|Fee Payment Plan]] page for details.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I cancel the Fee Payment Plan once enrolled?]]
   
If you decide you no longer wish to make installment payments under the Fee Payment Plan, simply make a lump sum payment for the remaining balance. This will fulfill the repayment agreement and the FPP will be complete for that term. Please note that the $60 participation fee will not be refunded.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|If my financial aid fully pays my tuition and fees, is there any benefit to enroll in the Fee Payment Plan?]]
   
No.
 
Financial aid will disburse and pay all charges reducing future FPP installments to zero. You will still be responsible for the $60 participation fee if you enroll.

# Frequently Asked Questions - Form 1098-T Tax Benefits Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/form-1098-t-tax-benefits](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/form-1098-t-tax-benefits)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Form 1098-T Tax Benefits
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|What is a 1098-T form?]]
   
The 1098-T form is used by eligible educational institutions to report information about their US resident students to the IRS as required by law. As an eligible educational institution, UC Berkeley reports certain financial and identifying information regarding US resident students for which UC Berkeley has received payments of "qualified education expenses" for the corresponding tax year. Included in the 1098-T form are qualified charges that were paid and financial assistance received for the corresponding tax year. Loans are excluded and not reported on the 1098-T form.
 
The 1098-T form is not intended to be used for determining any taxable income you may have received from scholarship or fellowship payments. The university does not report scholarship or fellowship income to you or to the IRS. Please use Worksheet 1-1 in [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) to figure the amount of a scholarship or fellowship grant you can exclude from gross income.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I get a copy of my 1098-T form?]]
   
If you have qualified paid charges and/or gift aid for the corresponding tax year, you may access your 1098-T form online in late January via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Which tax benefits do I qualify for?]]
   
UC Berkeley is unable to provide you with tax advice or to assist with strategies for filing your taxes. To determine your potential eligibility, please consult your tax advisor or the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Where can I find more information about the educational tax benefits?]]
   
For more information about the educational tax benefits, please visit the [IRS website(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/) or refer to [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will I know when my 1098-T form is available?]]
   
UC Berkeley will send you an email to the email address listed in [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). The email will come from [billingnotices@berkeley.edu(link sends e-mail)](mailto:billingnotices@berkeley.edu).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why did I not receive a form?]]
   
If your 1098-T tax form was not available after January 31st online via the [Tab Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx), if you did not consent to receiving the form online or withdrew consent, or if your 1098-T form was not mailed to you after February, a 1098-T form may not have been generated for you. Potential reasons for this are:
 
- The student was not billed qualified tuition related fees, or did not receive applicable scholarships or grants (i.e. intercampus visitor program or all courses were complimentary) for the tax year 
- The student took courses for which no academic credit is offered, even if the student is otherwise enrolled in a degree program
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I access my 1098-T forms from prior years?]]
   
Students may access their 1098-T forms for current and prior years via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx). Tab Services maintains records for 7 years.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if there is an error with the reported amounts shown?]]
   
Beginning with the tax year 2018 form, your 1098-T form reports qualified tuition related fee amounts paid in Box 1 for the calendar/tax year. Amounts paid are reported on your 1098-T form based on the date the payment is posted to your student account, regardless of the date or term the charge is posted. (Please note that mail-in or wire-transfer payments may experience a delay from the time they are received to the time they are posted on your student account). For example, a charge for the upcoming Spring that is posted to your student account in the current tax year, would be included on your tax form if the payment is posted to your student account by December 31 of the current tax year. However, if the payment is posted on or after January 1 of the next tax year, it would be included on the next year's form.
 
If you believe there is an error with the amount(s) reported on your form, please verify by reviewing your student account transactions on your [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) portal as well as your bank records. Please also review [IRS Publication 970 (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) to ensure that the payment in question qualifies as a Qualified Tuition Related Expense.
 
If you still believe there was an error, please [open a case with Billing and Payment Services(link is external)](https://csc-webtocase.sait-west.berkeley.edu/Case-Submit) under the topic 1098-T Form to have your form reviewed.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What are "qualified education expenses"?]]
   
The term "qualified education expenses" refers to the tuition and fees an individual is required to pay in order to enroll at or attend an eligible educational institution.
 
At UC Berkeley, this includes the following:
 
- Campus fee 
- Tuition 
- Non-resident tuition 
- Student services fee 
- Graduate professional student fees 
- Course material fees
 
The definition of “qualified education expenses” may differ depending on whether you are claiming the tax credit or taking a deduction. Please refer to the appropriate section in [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) for the related definition.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What expenses do not qualify as "qualified education expenses"?]]
   
Charges and fees associated with room, board, health insurance, student activities, athletics, books, equipment, transportation, and similar personal, living, or family expenses are not qualified expenses. Generally, amounts paid for any course or other educational expense involving sports, games, or hobbies are not eligible for the tax credit.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How can I find the details of the totals reported in boxes numbered 1-6 on my 1098-T form?]]
   
To find the details of the totals reported in boxes numbered 1-6 on your 1098-T form:
 
- Log in to the [TAB Services website(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/) 
- Click on 'View my 1098-T' in the upper left hand corner of the screen 
- Advance past page 1 of the 1098-T for detailed information
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if my legal name or SSN or ITIN is incorrect on my form?]]
   
If your SSN or ITIN number or legal name is incorrect, you must update by contacting the Office of the Registrar.
 
Please note: 1098-T forms will not be updated after the end of the reporting tax year. Forms are generated with the information on file as of December 31.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will I still receive a form if I do not have a SSN or ITIN?]]
   
If you do not have a SSN/ITIN to file with the university, (for example: an international student who does not have a SSN or ITIN) you may take no further action without penalties. You can still access your 1098-T online via the [TAB Services(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/) website, or receive one in the mail if you did not consent to receiving a 1098-T online, beginning late January for the previous tax year. The form will not have a SSN/ITIN reported on it.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if my SSN or ITIN is not on file with UC Berkeley?]]
   
If you do not have an existing SSN or ITIN to file with the university, no action is required.
 
If your existing SSN/ITIN is not yet registered with the university, you must submit your SSN or ITIN to UC Berkeley via your [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) portal profile link. If you are unable to update your information via the CalCentral portal profile link, please refer to [[SSN ITIN Solicitation and Other Student Data Student Billing|SSN/ITIN Solicitation and Other Student Data]] page for instructions on how to update your information. Your SSN/ITIN must be on file with the university prior to December 31 in order to have it reported on your form for that tax year.
 
Current federal tax regulations require the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) to report your Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), with other registration-related information, to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) on form 1098-T for each year that you are enrolled. To avoid penalties from the IRS, students should provide SSN’s or ITINs to UC Berkeley so that it may be included on the form 1098-T.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I register my existing SSN or ITIN with the university?]]
   
You can update your existing SSN or ITIN through your CalCentral profile by following these steps:
 
- Click the 'Update My SSN' button to add your SSN/ITIN to your profile 
- Enter your SSN/ITIN carefully
- Once the nformation is saved, you will not be able to make additional edits through CalCentral 
- Click the 'Update' button to save
      
### [[Home Student Billing|If I attend UC Berkeley Extension or Summer Session, will I receive a 1098-T form?]]
   
Yes.
 
UC Berkeley reports information on students who attend UC Berkeley Extension and/or Summer Session.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I am an international student. Do I qualify for these tax credits?]]
   
International students may not be eligible to claim the American Opportunity Credit or the Lifetime Learning Credit. To determine your potential eligibility, please consult your tax advisor or the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/). A 1098-T form will still be generated for you.

# Frequently Asked Questions - General Payments Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/general-payments](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/general-payments)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## General Payments
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I check if the payment I submitted has posted to my student account?]]
   
To check if your payment has posted to your student account, log in to [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) and click the 'My Finances' tab. Under the 'Billing Summary' section, click the 'View Transactions' button. In this view, click the 'Payments and Aid' tab to see all payments posted to your student account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I pay my bill using an outside agency scholarship?]]
   
If you would like to pay your bill using an outside agency scholarship, please submit the check to the [Financial Aid Office(link is external)](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/). They will process the scholarship as a credit to your account. Please allow 3 to 6 weeks for processing.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will my payment apply to my student account?]]
   
Payments on your student account will always apply in the order of due date, with the oldest charge first. If multiple charges on your student account have the same due date, payments will apply to your tuition and fees first. Payments cannot be targeted to pay a specific charge.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I change the payment amount when submitting an online payment?]]
   
You are able to pay the full balance due or a lesser amount through an online payment. For assistance, please see the instructions for [[Editing the Dollar Amount of an Online Payment Student Billing|Editing the Dollar Amount of your Online Payment]].
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I make a payment with my 529 Plan?]]
   
Coming in Spring 2021, students and delegates will have the option to pay their charges electronically via their 529 College Savings Plan. A $10.00 non-refundable convenience fee will apply to electronic 529 payments. Please see the [[529 Savings Plans Student Billing|list of participating 529 College Savings Plans that are available for use with Transact payments]].
 
If your plan is not listed, please contact your 529 Plan administrator in order to initiate the payment process.
 
Check payments should be sent to the address listed on the [[Check Payments Student Billing|Check Payments]] page.

# Frequently Asked Questions - General Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/general](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/general)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.296Z

## Content

## General
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I authorize my parent or other payer to view and discuss my account with UC Berkeley?]]
   
Parents or other payers must be authorized by the student in [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). Once authorized as a delegate in CalCentral, the parent or other payer will be able to make payments on the student account. Please allow 24 hours for access to the payment portal. Federal regulations and campus policy prohibit the release of information to a third party without student authorization. The process of granting authorization to release account information to a third party (for example, your parent or spouse) is initiated through CalCentral.
 
For more information, please refer to the [Student Authorization Delegate Set-up instruction guide(link is external)](https://sis.berkeley.edu/student-account-delegate) and/or the [campus policy on disclosure of student record information(link is external)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-policies-procedures/ferpa).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Do I need to give my parents (or other third party) authorization to discuss my account with UC Berkeley?]]
   
Federal regulations and campus policy prohibit the release of information to a third party without student authorization. If you would like to grant authorization to discuss and release account information to a third party (for example, your parents or spouse), please complete the [Grant Access FERPA Release(link is external)](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/share-information-parents-and-others). If you need assistance, please contact [Cal Student Central(link is external)](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/) located at 120 Sproul Hall or 510 664 9181.
 
For more information, please refer to the [campus policy on disclosure of student record information(link is external)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-policies-procedures/ferpa).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I was authorized as a delegate but I still cannot make an online payment. What should I do?]]
   
Once delegate access has been initiated by the student and accepted by the delegate, please allow 24 hours for access to the payment portal.
 
If after 24 hours you still are unable to make an online payment, contact Cal Student Central at 510 664 9181 or open a case online by visiting [Cal Student Central(link is external)](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/).
