# Frequently Asked Questions - International Payments Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/international-payments](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/international-payments)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## International Payments
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I make an international payment?]]
   
UC Berkeley has partnered with Flywire and Convera for international student payments and payment from a foreign country using US Dollars. Please refer to the following resources for more information and instructions:
 
- [[International Payments via Flywire Student Billing|International Payments via Flywire]] 
- [[International Payments via Convera Student Billing|International Payments via Convera]]
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I pay using foreign currency?]]
   
UC Berkeley has partnered with Flywire and Convera for international student payments and payment using foreign currency. Please refer to the following resources for more information and instructions:
 
- [[International Payments via Flywire Student Billing|International Payments via Flywire]] 
- [[International Payments via Convera Student Billing|International Payments via Convera]]
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What is UC Berkeley's account information?]]
   My bank says they have to wire funds directly to my school’s bank account.
When you send funds through Flywire or Convera, you are sending funds to UC Berkeley. Flywire, and Convera acting as our agent, processes your payment and delivers it directly to us in the destination currency along with your student information for accurate posting. This is how UC Berkeley receives wire transfer payments from outside of the US.
 
Attempting to send wire transfers without utilizing Flywire or Convera will cause delays in UC Berkeley receiving your payment and updating your student account. Additional fees may also apply.
 
Please initiate your payment through your Cal Central portal. For bank transfer options, once you initiate the payment, you will receive payment instructions with an authorization letter permitting your bank to send the funds via Flywire or Convera. If your bank has any questions, Flywire's and Convera's support can help.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What are UC Berkeley's bank wire details?]]
   
You can obtain UC Berkeley's bank wire details by first initiating your payment on your Cal Central student portal via CashNet, and then selecting either Flywire or Convera. Once you initiate your payment, the bank information will be displayed with instructions on how to send your payment.
 
International payments to UC Berkeley are managed by Flywire and Convera to ensure funds are received promptly and securely. Both options will process and deliver your payment directly to UC Berkeley with your student information for accurate posting.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I pay from a foreign country using US Dollars?]]
   
UC Berkeley has partnered with Flywire and Convera for international student payments and payment from a foreign country using US Dollars. Please refer to the following resources for more information and instructions:
 
- [[International Payments via Flywire Student Billing|International Payments via Flywire]] 
- [[International Payments via Convera Student Billing|International Payments via Convera]]
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Does UC Berkeley accept direct wire payments?]]
   
Please note that UC Berkeley does not accept direct wire payments from students. Wire transfers intended for student payments must be remitted through Flywire or Convera, which will ensure that your payment is posted to your account correctly and timely.
 
Please refer to the following two options for International Payments:
 
- [[International Payments via Flywire Student Billing|International Payments via Flywire]] 
- [[International Payments via Convera Student Billing|International Payments via Convera]]
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What is Flywire, and is it safe to use?]]
   
Yes, Flywire is a secure and convenient way to make international payments to UC Berkeley. Flywire allows you to track your payment online from start to finish, leverage 24/7 multi-lingual customer support, and access competitive exchange rates.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Does Flywire charge fees?]]
   Flywire's exchange rates seem higher than what I can find online.
The exchange rates you may find online are mid-market rates, which are not available to individuals. Instead, mid-market rates are the published rates for currency purchases for large volume traders.
 
Please reach out to Flywire's customer service team with any pricing concerns. If you have found a lower rate with your bank for local bank transfer payments, Flywire offers a best rate guarantee that will match your bank's offer.
 
Please refer to the [Best Price Guarantee for Bank Transfers(link is external)](https://www.flywire.com/legal/best-price-guarantee) page on the Flywire website for more information.

# Frequently Asked Questions - Student Financial Agreement (SFA) Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/student-financial-agreement-sfa](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/student-financial-agreement-sfa)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.296Z

## Content

## Student Financial Agreement (SFA)
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|What is the Student Financial Agreement (SFA)?]]
   
The Student Financial Agreement (SFA) provides important information to students about the financial policies associated with their enrollment at UC Berkeley. Tuition and fee charges are incurred through enrollment and other charges post to student accounts throughout the semester. The SFA sets forth expectations for making payment on charges when they are due. We feel it is important that students understand and acknowledge their financial responsibilities when it comes to the charges on their student account. This document also addresses the policies related to, among other things, non-payment, communications, and student privacy (FERPA).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why do I have to sign the Student Financial Agreement?]]
   
Our goal is to help our students understand the cost of their education and the financial policies associated with their enrollment at UC Berkeley. The Student Financial Agreement is another means for the university to be transparent about our policies and requirements. This agreement, in conjunction with university websites and communications, help define the university’s expectations for payment, and allows us to clearly inform students of related policies.
 
While most of our students do pay their bills, we do see students who leave the university with unpaid charges, not fully recognizing the consequences. Once students have left the university, they may not have access to the same types of resources that could help them resolve their unpaid charges.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What happens if I refuse to sign the Student Financial Agreement?]]
   
The Student Financial Agreement serves as notification of potential consequences of non-payment and provides important policy information. If a student chooses not to complete the SFA, they will not be able to enroll in classes. Once the agreement is completed for the academic year, the restriction will be removed and the student will be able to begin enrollment.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Do other institutions have this type of agreement?]]
   
Yes, it is a common practice among higher education institutions across the United States, including other campuses in the UC System. It is consistent with the national movement to increase financial literacy among college students.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Does the SFA have to be completed if financial aid or a third party contract covers the cost of tuition?]]
   
All students must complete the Student Financial Agreement once each academic year.
 
Certain eligibility is required and must be maintained in order to have tuition and fees covered by other means. Students are ultimately responsible for all tuition and fees. If a student's financial aid amount is reduced or the third party agency has not paid tuition and fees, the student is required to pay remaining charges on their student account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why must I complete the SFA if my tuition and applicable fees are being covered by the university or outside funding sources?]]
   
It is possible that students receiving university funding may accrue charges on their account which are not directly covered by the university and/or outside sources of aid. For instance, students may be sponsored for tuition and fees only, and have housing and UHS charges, for which they are responsible. Students are financially responsible for those additional charges and, as such, must accept the SFA. Additionally, in the event an account balance results from a change of circumstance in a funding source, students are responsible for the amount due.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will completing the SFA affect my financial aid eligibility?]]
   
No.
 
The SFA is independent of your financial aid, and completing the agreement will not have an impact on the aid you are awarded.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|My parents pay my tuition. Can they complete the form?]]
   
No.
 
While payment by a third party is acceptable, it is the enrolled student who is ultimately responsible for agreeing to the Student Financial Agreement.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Where can I find the Student Financial Agreement?]]
   
To navigate to the Student Financial Agreement, first log in to CalCentral.
 
Then, from the My Dashboard page, there will be listed any 'Incomplete' tasks that require action, which will include the SFA that has not yet been submitted.
 
SFA's that have already been submitted will be listed under 'Complete' tasks.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|When will the Student Financial Agreement be assigned?]]
   
The Student Financial Agreement will be assigned to all active students prior to the beginning of enrollment for the fall term, every academic year for the duration of their studies.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How soon can I enroll after completing the Student Financial Agreement?]]
   
Once you submit the agreement, you will be able to begin the enrollment process.

# Frequently Asked Questions - Tuition Insurance Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/tuition-insurance](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq/tuition-insurance)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.297Z

## Content

## Tuition Insurance
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why is the university making Tuition Insurance available?]]
   
The cost of going to UC Berkeley has skyrocketed in recent years, to the point where most families suffer a serious financial loss if their student has to medically withdraw. Tuition Insurance is one option families can use to reduce their risk of financial loss due to non-attendance.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is Tuition Insurance required?]]
   
No.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I get Tuition Insurance elsewhere if I wish?]]
   
Yes.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What does Tuition Insurance cover?]]
   
- Medical withdrawal (100% of benefit) 
- Mental or nervous condition leading to medical withdrawal (100% of benefit) 
- Death of the student (100% of benefit) 
- Death of tuition payer (if different from student) that leads to withdrawal (100% of benefit)
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How much does Tuition Insurance cost?]]
   
It depends on how much coverage you want. In-state undergraduates will probably want to purchase less coverage than out-of-state graduate students going to a professional school, where fees are much higher. The cost is approximately 1% of the coverage you wish to insure or your invoice amount. For example, coverage for a $20,000 student invoice would be $220.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Who is eligible for coverage?]]
   
Any student currently enrolled at UC Berkeley is eligible for coverage. Extension students are not eligible for coverage.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I have a disability or a pre-existing condition?]]
   
The policy does not have a pre-existing condition clause. However, the policy excludes illness or injuries that are active at the time of enrollment. For instance, if a student is being treated for pneumonia at the time of enrollment, forcing a withdrawal two weeks later, coverage would be denied.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I have to leave during the semester due to pregnancy?]]
   
If the pregnancy leads to medical complications that require you to withdraw, you will be covered.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What gets reimbursed if I file a claim?]]
   
The cost of attendance, including:
 
- Tuition 
- Room and Board 
- Fees 
- Other applicable fees as shown on the invoice such as: 
- Activity Fees 
- Course Material Fee 
- Orientation Fee, etc.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is there a deductible?]]
   
The policy does not have a deductible. However, the amount of payment will be reduced by any refund provided to you by the registrar or other campus offices.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I file a claim?]]
   
To file a claim, notify the insurance carrier within 30 days of the loss or as soon as possible. The claims department will provide a claim number and claim forms to be filled out by the student. Please call the Claims Department at 888-427-5045 (please have your Policy number on hand).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|When can I purchase coverage?]]
   
You may purchase coverage anytime prior to the start of the term you are purchasing for. Please keep in mind, however, that if the symptoms that force you to medically withdraw are already present when you buy coverage, the insurance will not apply.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How long does the policy last?]]
   
The coverage period are the dates for the academic term.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is summer school covered?]]
   
Yes. Please visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website to purchase coverage for summer sessions.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I spend the semester abroad? Am I still covered?]]
   
As long as you are registered at UC Berkeley for that semester, you are covered wherever you are studying.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I purchase coverage for just one semester?]]
   
Yes, you have the choice to purchase for one semester or several.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I obtain coverage?]]
   
To obtain coverage, please visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website, or call GradGuard at 877-794-6603.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How can I purchase Tuition Insurance?]]
   
You can purchase Tuition Insurance via the Transact Portal when remitting a payment, or by visiting the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I declined GradGuard how can I go back and purchase?]]
   
You have the option to purchase Tuition Insurance up to the first day of instruction for the term. If you originally declined, you can visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website to purchase.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I purchase Tuition Insurance for the Summer Term?]]
   
Yes, Tuition Insurance is offered for the Summer Term.

# Frequently Asked Questions Student Billing

- **Source URL**: [https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq-page](https://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/faq-page)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T07:34:43.296Z

## Content

## General
 [[Home Student Billing|collapse all]] [[Home Student Billing|expand all]]      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I authorize my parent or other payer to view and discuss my account with UC Berkeley?]]
   
Parents or other payers must be authorized by the student in [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). Once authorized as a delegate in CalCentral, the parent or other payer will be able to make payments on the student account. Please allow 24 hours for access to the payment portal. Federal regulations and campus policy prohibit the release of information to a third party without student authorization. The process of granting authorization to release account information to a third party (for example, your parent or spouse) is initiated through CalCentral.
 
For more information, please refer to the [Student Authorization Delegate Set-up instruction guide(link is external)](https://sis.berkeley.edu/student-account-delegate) and/or the [campus policy on disclosure of student record information(link is external)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-policies-procedures/ferpa).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Do I need to give my parents (or other third party) authorization to discuss my account with UC Berkeley?]]
   
Federal regulations and campus policy prohibit the release of information to a third party without student authorization. If you would like to grant authorization to discuss and release account information to a third party (for example, your parents or spouse), please complete the [Grant Access FERPA Release(link is external)](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/share-information-parents-and-others). If you need assistance, please contact [Cal Student Central(link is external)](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/) located at 120 Sproul Hall or 510 664 9181.
 
For more information, please refer to the [campus policy on disclosure of student record information(link is external)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-policies-procedures/ferpa).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I was authorized as a delegate but I still cannot make an online payment. What should I do?]]
   
Once delegate access has been initiated by the student and accepted by the delegate, please allow 24 hours for access to the payment portal.
 
If after 24 hours you still are unable to make an online payment, contact Cal Student Central at 510 664 9181 or open a case online by visiting [Cal Student Central(link is external)](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/).

## Charges and Fees
       
### [[Home Student Billing|How will students pay for access?]]
   
The access charge for Inclusive Access materials will be added to your student billing account after the drop/add deadline, which is around the 5th week of the semester. The charge will appear as Bookstore – Inclusive Access. Students who opt out by the posted deadline for the current term will not be billed.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I'm no longer an active student. How can I view my student account?]]
   
For information on how to view your account, please review the [Alumni and Non-Current Student(link is external)](https://sis.berkeley.edu/alumni-and-non-current-students) job aid.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will my fees be different depending on the mode of instruction?]]
   
Some or all instruction for all or part of the Academic Year may be delivered remotely. Figures for tuition and fees represent currently approved amounts and may not be final. ## Fee Payment Plan (FPP)
       
### [[Home Student Billing|I enrolled in the Fee Payment Plan last semester. Do I need to enroll in the plan each semester?]]
   
Yes. You must enroll in the Fee Payment Plan each fall and spring semester. The option to pay in installments is not available for Summer Session and for some programs. To learn more about this payment option, visit the [[Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing|Fee Payment Plan]] page.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can someone other than the student activate the Fee Payment Plan?]]
   
No.
 
Only a student can activate the Fee Payment Plan through [Cal Central(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). While a student may give a parent/other person delegate access to view financials and pay bills, only the student can activate the FPP.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Do I need to make a payment to activate the plan?]]
   
No.
 
After activating the Fee Payment Plan, you must pay an amount equal to the first installment by the Friday prior to term instruction to avoid cancellation. If a payment is made before the FPP is activated, the FPP will recalculate based on the new principal balance due, and the first installment payment will still be required.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I have partial financial aid and want to be on the Fee Payment Plan. Do I need to make a payment to activate the FPP?]]
   
No.
 
Payment will not be required to activate the Fee Payment Plan. Financial aid will reduce the balance, and the FPP will recalculate based on the new balance. The 5 payment installments will adjust accordingly.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I mail in my payment. Can someone at UC Berkeley activate the Fee Payment Plan for me?]]
   
No.
 
In order to participate in the Fee Payment Plan, you must complete the process online.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What happens if I don’t pay my installment by the due date?]]
   
If you do not make payment according to the due dates outlined in your Installment Schedule, you may incur late fees and have a block placed on your account.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is the Fee Payment Plan participation fee refundable?]]
   
No.
 
You will be charged a non-refundable $60 fee to participate in the Fee Payment Plan.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I set up the Fee Payment Plan for the whole academic year?]]
   
No.
 
You are not able to enroll in the FPP for the full academic year. You can only enroll in the Fee Payment Plan at the beginning of each term. Please visit the Enrollment section on the [[Fee Payment Plan (FPP) Student Billing|Fee Payment Plan]] page for details.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I cancel the Fee Payment Plan once enrolled?]]
   
If you decide you no longer wish to make installment payments under the Fee Payment Plan, simply make a lump sum payment for the remaining balance. This will fulfill the repayment agreement and the FPP will be complete for that term. Please note that the $60 participation fee will not be refunded.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|If my financial aid fully pays my tuition and fees, is there any benefit to enroll in the Fee Payment Plan?]]
   
No.
 
Financial aid will disburse and pay all charges reducing future FPP installments to zero. You will still be responsible for the $60 participation fee if you enroll.

## Form 1098-T Tax Benefits
       
### [[Home Student Billing|What is a 1098-T form?]]
   
The 1098-T form is used by eligible educational institutions to report information about their US resident students to the IRS as required by law. As an eligible educational institution, UC Berkeley reports certain financial and identifying information regarding US resident students for which UC Berkeley has received payments of "qualified education expenses" for the corresponding tax year. Included in the 1098-T form are qualified charges that were paid and financial assistance received for the corresponding tax year. Loans are excluded and not reported on the 1098-T form.
 
The 1098-T form is not intended to be used for determining any taxable income you may have received from scholarship or fellowship payments. The university does not report scholarship or fellowship income to you or to the IRS. Please use Worksheet 1-1 in [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) to figure the amount of a scholarship or fellowship grant you can exclude from gross income.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I get a copy of my 1098-T form?]]
   
If you have qualified paid charges and/or gift aid for the corresponding tax year, you may access your 1098-T form online in late January via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Which tax benefits do I qualify for?]]
   
UC Berkeley is unable to provide you with tax advice or to assist with strategies for filing your taxes. To determine your potential eligibility, please consult your tax advisor or the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Where can I find more information about the educational tax benefits?]]
   
For more information about the educational tax benefits, please visit the [IRS website(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/) or refer to [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How will I know when my 1098-T form is available?]]
   
UC Berkeley will send you an email to the email address listed in [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). The email will come from [billingnotices@berkeley.edu(link sends e-mail)](mailto:billingnotices@berkeley.edu).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Why did I not receive a form?]]
   
If your 1098-T tax form was not available after January 31st online via the [Tab Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx), if you did not consent to receiving the form online or withdrew consent, or if your 1098-T form was not mailed to you after February, a 1098-T form may not have been generated for you. Potential reasons for this are:
 
- The student was not billed qualified tuition related fees, or did not receive applicable scholarships or grants (i.e. intercampus visitor program or all courses were complimentary) for the tax year 
- The student took courses for which no academic credit is offered, even if the student is otherwise enrolled in a degree program
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I access my 1098-T forms from prior years?]]
   
Students may access their 1098-T forms for current and prior years via the [TAB Services website(link is external)](https://www.tsc1099.com/Login1098.aspx). Tab Services maintains records for 7 years.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if there is an error with the reported amounts shown?]]
   
Beginning with the tax year 2018 form, your 1098-T form reports qualified tuition related fee amounts paid in Box 1 for the calendar/tax year. Amounts paid are reported on your 1098-T form based on the date the payment is posted to your student account, regardless of the date or term the charge is posted. (Please note that mail-in or wire-transfer payments may experience a delay from the time they are received to the time they are posted on your student account). For example, a charge for the upcoming Spring that is posted to your student account in the current tax year, would be included on your tax form if the payment is posted to your student account by December 31 of the current tax year. However, if the payment is posted on or after January 1 of the next tax year, it would be included on the next year's form.
 
If you believe there is an error with the amount(s) reported on your form, please verify by reviewing your student account transactions on your [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) portal as well as your bank records. Please also review [IRS Publication 970 (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) to ensure that the payment in question qualifies as a Qualified Tuition Related Expense.
 
If you still believe there was an error, please [open a case with Billing and Payment Services(link is external)](https://csc-webtocase.sait-west.berkeley.edu/Case-Submit) under the topic 1098-T Form to have your form reviewed.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What are "qualified education expenses"?]]
   
The term "qualified education expenses" refers to the tuition and fees an individual is required to pay in order to enroll at or attend an eligible educational institution.
 
At UC Berkeley, this includes the following:
 
- Campus fee 
- Tuition 
- Non-resident tuition 
- Student services fee 
- Graduate professional student fees 
- Course material fees
 
The definition of “qualified education expenses” may differ depending on whether you are claiming the tax credit or taking a deduction. Please refer to the appropriate section in [IRS Publication 970 (Tax Benefits for Education) (PDF file)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf) for the related definition.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What expenses do not qualify as "qualified education expenses"?]]
   
Charges and fees associated with room, board, health insurance, student activities, athletics, books, equipment, transportation, and similar personal, living, or family expenses are not qualified expenses. Generally, amounts paid for any course or other educational expense involving sports, games, or hobbies are not eligible for the tax credit.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How can I find the details of the totals reported in boxes numbered 1-6 on my 1098-T form?]]
   
To find the details of the totals reported in boxes numbered 1-6 on your 1098-T form:
 
- Log in to the [TAB Services website(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/) 
- Click on 'View my 1098-T' in the upper left hand corner of the screen 
- Advance past page 1 of the 1098-T for detailed information
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if my legal name or SSN or ITIN is incorrect on my form?]]
   
If your SSN or ITIN number or legal name is incorrect, you must update by contacting the Office of the Registrar.
 
Please note: 1098-T forms will not be updated after the end of the reporting tax year. Forms are generated with the information on file as of December 31.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Will I still receive a form if I do not have a SSN or ITIN?]]
   
If you do not have a SSN/ITIN to file with the university, (for example: an international student who does not have a SSN or ITIN) you may take no further action without penalties. You can still access your 1098-T online via the [TAB Services(link is external)](http://www.tsc1098t.com/) website, or receive one in the mail if you did not consent to receiving a 1098-T online, beginning late January for the previous tax year. The form will not have a SSN/ITIN reported on it.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What should I do if my SSN or ITIN is not on file with UC Berkeley?]]
   
If you do not have an existing SSN or ITIN to file with the university, no action is required.
 
If your existing SSN/ITIN is not yet registered with the university, you must submit your SSN or ITIN to UC Berkeley via your [CalCentral(link is external)](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) portal profile link. If you are unable to update your information via the CalCentral portal profile link, please refer to [[SSN ITIN Solicitation and Other Student Data Student Billing|SSN/ITIN Solicitation and Other Student Data]] page for instructions on how to update your information. Your SSN/ITIN must be on file with the university prior to December 31 in order to have it reported on your form for that tax year.
 
Current federal tax regulations require the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) to report your Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), with other registration-related information, to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) on form 1098-T for each year that you are enrolled. To avoid penalties from the IRS, students should provide SSN’s or ITINs to UC Berkeley so that it may be included on the form 1098-T.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I register my existing SSN or ITIN with the university?]]

### [[Home Student Billing|If I attend UC Berkeley Extension or Summer Session, will I receive a 1098-T form?]]
   
Yes.
 
UC Berkeley reports information on students who attend UC Berkeley Extension and/or Summer Session.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I am an international student. Do I qualify for these tax credits?]]
   
International students may not be eligible to claim the American Opportunity Credit or the Lifetime Learning Credit. To determine your potential eligibility, please consult your tax advisor or the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)(link is external)](https://www.irs.gov/). A 1098-T form will still be generated for you.
               
## Tuition Insurance
       
### [[Home Student Billing|Why is the university making Tuition Insurance available?]]
   
The cost of going to UC Berkeley has skyrocketed in recent years, to the point where most families suffer a serious financial loss if their student has to medically withdraw. Tuition Insurance is one option families can use to reduce their risk of financial loss due to non-attendance.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is Tuition Insurance required?]]
   
No.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I get Tuition Insurance elsewhere if I wish?]]
   
Yes.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What does Tuition Insurance cover?]]
   
- Medical withdrawal (100% of benefit) 
- Mental or nervous condition leading to medical withdrawal (100% of benefit) 
- Death of the student (100% of benefit) 
- Death of tuition payer (if different from student) that leads to withdrawal (100% of benefit)
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How much does Tuition Insurance cost?]]
   
It depends on how much coverage you want. In-state undergraduates will probably want to purchase less coverage than out-of-state graduate students going to a professional school, where fees are much higher. The cost is approximately 1% of the coverage you wish to insure or your invoice amount. For example, coverage for a $20,000 student invoice would be $220.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Who is eligible for coverage?]]
   
Any student currently enrolled at UC Berkeley is eligible for coverage. Extension students are not eligible for coverage.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I have a disability or a pre-existing condition?]]
   
The policy does not have a pre-existing condition clause. However, the policy excludes illness or injuries that are active at the time of enrollment. For instance, if a student is being treated for pneumonia at the time of enrollment, forcing a withdrawal two weeks later, coverage would be denied.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I have to leave during the semester due to pregnancy?]]
   
If the pregnancy leads to medical complications that require you to withdraw, you will be covered.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What gets reimbursed if I file a claim?]]
   
The cost of attendance, including:
 
- Tuition 
- Room and Board 
- Fees 
- Other applicable fees as shown on the invoice such as: 
- Activity Fees 
- Course Material Fee 
- Orientation Fee, etc.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is there a deductible?]]
   
The policy does not have a deductible. However, the amount of payment will be reduced by any refund provided to you by the registrar or other campus offices.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I file a claim?]]
   
To file a claim, notify the insurance carrier within 30 days of the loss or as soon as possible. The claims department will provide a claim number and claim forms to be filled out by the student. Please call the Claims Department at 888-427-5045 (please have your Policy number on hand).
      
### [[Home Student Billing|When can I purchase coverage?]]
   
You may purchase coverage anytime prior to the start of the term you are purchasing for. Please keep in mind, however, that if the symptoms that force you to medically withdraw are already present when you buy coverage, the insurance will not apply.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How long does the policy last?]]
   
The coverage period are the dates for the academic term.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Is summer school covered?]]
   
Yes. Please visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website to purchase coverage for summer sessions.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|What if I spend the semester abroad? Am I still covered?]]
   
As long as you are registered at UC Berkeley for that semester, you are covered wherever you are studying.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I purchase coverage for just one semester?]]
   
Yes, you have the choice to purchase for one semester or several.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How do I obtain coverage?]]
   
To obtain coverage, please visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website, or call GradGuard at 877-794-6603.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|How can I purchase Tuition Insurance?]]
   
You can purchase Tuition Insurance via the Transact Portal when remitting a payment, or by visiting the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|I declined GradGuard how can I go back and purchase?]]
   
You have the option to purchase Tuition Insurance up to the first day of instruction for the term. If you originally declined, you can visit the [GradGuard(link is external)](https://gradguard.com/tuition/berkeley) website to purchase.
      
### [[Home Student Billing|Can I purchase Tuition Insurance for the Summer Term?]]
   
Yes, Tuition Insurance is offered for the Summer Term.

# GBO Check-In - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/gbo-check-in](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/golden-bear-orientation-overview/gbo-check-in)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.642Z

## Content

*updated July 2, 2026*
 
## Check-In
 
Note: The information on this page may be updated frequently throughout the semester.
 
Your first important (read: mandatory!) step in Golden Bear Orientation is Check-In.
 
Here’s what you need to know.
 
### Where and When to Check-In (University-Owned Resident Hall* Students):
 
If you are living in University-Owned Residence Halls/Apartments, you can check into GBO at the same location you received your keys to your new home! University Housing will be providing details about your specific [Move In Date and Location](https://housing.berkeley.edu/living-on-campus/move-in/) via your Berkeley email. Regardless of your Move In date, GBO Check In will occur on Wednesday, August 19, 2026.
 
### Where and When to Check-In (Enclave, Panoramic, University Village, International House and non-University Owned Spaces)
 
If you are living in Enclave, Panoramic, University Village, International House or a non-University owned space, you will check into GBO on Wednesday, August 19, 2026 between 9:00am and 6:00pm at Lower Sproul Plaza. You’ll only need to come once!
     
**Housing Status**
   
**GBO Check-In Date & Time**
   
**GBO Check-In Location**
     
University-Owned Residence Halls/Apartments*
   
Wednesday August 19th
 
9:00am-5:00pm
   
Assigned Residence Hall/Apartment – look for the table under the “Orientation” tent
     
Commuter (Non-University Owned Spaces), International House, Enclave, Panoramic and University Village Students
   
Wednesday, August 19th
 
9:00am-6:00pm
   
Lower Sproul Plaza
     
*Unit 1, Unit 2, Unit 3, Foothill, Stern, Clark Kerr, Anchor House, Max Martinez Commons, Channing Bowditch, New Sequoia, Blackwell
 
### What to Bring to Check In
 
Bring a valid ID (state ID, drivers license, and/or passport). That’s it!
 
### What to You Will Get at Check In
 
During GBO Check-In, you will get:
 
- Your GBO nametag, wristband, and clear drawstring bag, which will grant you access to events including meals. 
- If you’re living in Non-University Owned Spaces: Your Cal 1 Card and [AC Transit BayPass.](https://pt.berkeley.edu/StudentEasypass) (If you live in a Res Hall, you’ll get your Cal 1 Card when you move in.) 
- Details about GBO programming, including when to arrive on Thursday and how you will meet your GBO small group will be sent via email on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Check out [[GBO Sample Schedule - Golden Bear Orientation|GBO Sample Schedules]] here, but remember that each GBO small group has a unique schedule.
 
### Parking & University Residence Hall Move In
 
University Residence Hall Move In will take place over several days during the week of **August 17, 2026**. There may be adjusted street parking hours/limits due to Housing Move In. There are campus-owned parking structures at multiple locations around central campus, as well as a parking lot directly under the MLK Student Union building. View the [Campus Parking site](https://pt.berkeley.edu/parking), as well as the [Student Permit process](https://pt.berkeley.edu/StudentParking). There are also public parking lots surrounding campus. You may have lots of items in your car as you start your Berkeley career; we encourage you to not leave valuables in your car and complete the move into your Berkeley residence prior to GBO Check In.
 
**If you have Move-In questions:** Review the [Housing Move-In](https://housing.berkeley.edu/living-on-campus/move-in/) page and follow instructions emailed to your new berkeley.edu email.

## Content

*Updated March 20, 2026*
 

 

 
You might be wondering: what will Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) look like? Below are two sample schedules for GBO Fall 2026 transfer students and first year students. The majority of programs during GBO are not held with the entire incoming class together and each GBO Small Group (over 250 of them!) are unique to provide personalized programming and ensure access to mealtimes. You will receive your specific schedule on the first day of GBO programming (Thursday, August 20) from your Orientation Leaders (OLs).
 
We understand that a model built for so many students will not accommodate every individual; if after reading through the sample schedules below you believe that you will need accommodations during GBO, please scroll to the bottom of this page* to find more information on how to request these accommodations.
 
See below for sample schedules based on your admit type.

## First Year Student Fall 2026 Golden Bear Orientation Sample Schedule

## *Note
 
We recognize that a model built for so many students will not accommodate everyone. Please read over our [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|**policies**]] for more information about participation requirements, and to let us know how we can best serve your needs for orientation.
 
## Check In
 
Check In will occur on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Check back in May for further details about [[GBO Check-In - Golden Bear Orientation|Check In]], including locations and times. We are working on new ideas for Fall 2026 to reduce lines and improve how we serve you during such a busy time.
 
## Meals
 
Meals will be provided throughout GBO. You will have an assigned location and time for each meal. All meals will be able to provide options for dietary needs. If you do not see your dietary needs met, please directly ask one of the Cal Dining Staff present and inform your Orientation Leader as soon as possible.
 
Our Dining Options Include:
 
- **Berkeley Dining @ The Residence Halls:**The majority of your meals will be served at various Berkeley dining facilities located throughout the residential communities. Your schedule will be designed to allow you to explore different on-campus eateries over the five days, guided by your Orientation Leader. 
- **Bite of Berkeley:**You will have one meal that allows you to sample local flavors from the Telegraph Avenue neighborhood, through collaborations with local restaurants. These eateries prepare a special, quick-service menu for GBO, offering dine-in or take-out depending on the restaurant’s size. 
- **Food Trucks at the Campanile:**To efficiently feed 9,000 students daily, we utilize an excellent team of food trucks that allow all orientation groups to enjoy at least one picnic meal on the beautiful Campanile Esplanade.
 
Curious about what dietary restrictions can be accommodated? Please refer to our [[FAQS - Golden Bear Orientation|Frequently Asked Questions page]].
 
## Grouping, GBO Small Group Time & OL Choice
 
GBO Programming will begin on Thursday, August 20 by meeting your Orientation Leaders (OLs) and other new students in your GBO small group at Grouping. You will be with this group throughout GBO excluding College Programming on Monday. Students will engage in dialogue and community building with a small group of their peers and Orientation Leaders (OLs). OL Choice are times when your OLs will select programming specifically for your group.
 
## New Student Welcome
 
Check back in June for updated details on the New Student Welcome.
 
## Bear Foundations
 
Bear Foundations is a Golden Bear Orientation program designed to introduce new students to conversations about identity, community, belonging and inclusion at UC Berkeley. Through a large group experience students engage with the UC Berkeley Principles of Community, reflect on their own identities and experiences and learn from stories and perspectives of others.
 
The program encourages students to recognize their role in fostering a respectful, welcoming and inclusive campus community while continuing to explore identity, dialogue and community building throughout their time at Berkeley.
 
## Bear Pact
 
Bear Pact is a **mandatory**performance that will teach you about important issues faced by college students: sexual violence and harassment, related policies, reporting options and resources, mental health, bystander intervention, alcohol and substance use. Learn about the many ways you can maintain a balanced lifestyle and the resources on campus that can help you in this pursuit. You will also gain strategies to take care of friends, classmates, and roommates.
 
## Late Night Programming
 
Check back in May for updated details on Late Night Programming.
 
## Resource Fair
 
The Campus Department Resource Fair will introduce incoming students to 70+ campus departments, including Berkeley Study Abroad and University Health Services. The fair will be hosted in person and will allow you to connect directly with staff from various campus departments.
 
## Transfer Symposium
 
Check back in May for updated details on the Transfer Symposium.
 
## Bears in the Bay
 
Your Berkeley experience extends beyond the campus and we know many of you are eager to explore the Bay Area. Bears in the Bay will take you to a venue in the Bay Area (past excursions have included SF MOMA, the Exploratorium, Oakland Museum, Bubble Planet). All transportation and tickets will be included.
 
Bay Area excursions will be assigned for individual GBO small groups. Transfers/UCEAP students will participate on Friday, August 21 and first years will participate either Saturday, August 22 or Sunday August 23.
 
## Bite of Berkeley
 
We are surrounded by incredible and varied food options in the city of Berkeley. Exploring those is built into GBO! You and your small group will be assigned to visit a local restaurant for one of your lunch or dinner blocks during GBO.
 
## Transfer Student Welcome
 
Transfer Student Welcome is a program in partnership with the Transfer Center, with its main goal being to welcome all transfer students to the Berkeley community and to discuss services and resources available to them.
 
## Alumni Mixer
 
Transfer students will have the opportunity to learn career tips and information from alumni working in different industries. Check back in May for more details on the Alumni Mixer.
 
## College Programming
 
College Programming consists of programming designed by each college (e.g College of Letters and Science, College of Natural Resources) to prepare students for life in that specific academic environment. During these events, there will be an introduction to your college and more specific sessions centered around what to expect from your college and major. Check the Cal Events app for specific events related to your major.**Note: EAP students should not attend College Programming.**
 
## Affinity Spaces
 
Build community with fellow new students who share your identity! Affinity spaces are informal, social spaces for students from diverse backgrounds. You’ll also have the opportunity to meet staff and/or continuing students. You can self-select which social(s) to attend, or choose not to attend any, and you do not need to attend with your small group. Descriptions of each Affinity Space are available in the Cal Events app.
 
## Banner Signing
 
An iconic GBO tradition! Come add your name to the Class of 2028 or Class of 2030 banners. These will be hung up at your graduation – book ends to your Berkeley career!
 
## Group Closing
 
All good things must come to an end, and GBO is no exception. Closing with small groups and Orientation Leaders is an opportunity to wrap up the week and look to the coming semester. The group closing will include dinner.

# Getting Started - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/getting-started](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/golden-bear-experience/getting-started)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.641Z

## Content

Here are some basic steps to get your Berkeley career off to a great start.
 
## Log into CalCentral
 
![CalCentral](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/calcentral-386x240-300x187.png) This student portal is where you will find instructions, dates, contact information, and tasks for you as an incoming student. The tasks below will be listed within [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
 
## Create your CalNet ID and bConnected account
 
![CalNet ID login](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/CalNet-login-386x291-300x226.png)Your CalNet ID and password are essential to accessing Berkeley online systems and tools. New students receive an invitation to do this from the Registrar. Once you’ve created your CalNet ID, you will also need to [set up your bConnected account](https://bconnected.berkeley.edu/) (Berkeley’s email, calendar, and file sharing system). Remember that much of the communication you receive as a new student will come to your Berkeley email address.
 

 
## Apply for Housing
 
![Housing website](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/housing-386x291-300x226.png) The [housing application](https://portal.housing.berkeley.edu/StarRezPortalx/DBA27648/1/1/Home-Home) deadline for Spring 2026 students in October 1. Be sure to learn about the application process and your housing options, costs, and deadlines, via the [Housing website](http://housing.berkeley.edu/).
 
## Review Financial Aid & Scholarship Information
 
![Review financial aid and scholarship information](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/CalCentral-finance-386x291-1-300x226.png) [Take a careful look at your estimated cost of attendance and any aid or scholarships](http://financialaid.berkeley.edu/tags/my-finances) that have been offered to you via MyFinances in [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
 
## Submit Final Transcript
 
![Submit final transcript](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/UCB_day1_high_resolution_files_UCOP-46-cropped-386x291-300x226.jpg) Be sure to [send an official and final version of your transcript](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) to the Office of Undergraduate Admissions by the deadline. This information is included both in [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) and in your Conditions of Admission.
 
## Begin Process for Cal 1 Card & AC Transit Clipper Card
 
![C1C New Design](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/C1C_New-Design-2.jpg)The Cal 1 Card serves as your official university identification. (Cal 1 Card issuance requires that you submit a photo online; you’ll find directions in [CalCentral](http://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).) Also, as a student, you’re provided with an AC Transit Class Pass, which allows you free access to all AC Transit bus routes and can be used for other public transportation, such as BART. When you arrive on campus you will be given both your Cal 1 Card and your AC transit Class Pass Clipper card. You’ll find details in[CalCentral](http://calcentral.berkeley.edu).
 
## Complete Immunization & Health Insurance Enrollment
 
![University Health Services](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/uhs-gbo-1-300x226.png)All incoming UC Berkeley students are required to comply with the [immunization and TB screening mandate](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/requirements)by December 31, 2025, prior to coming to campus. All students attending any University of California school are required to meet the COVID-19 vaccine requirement prior to enrolling in classes. Follow the instructions from [University Health Services](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/requirements/covid19). Also, be sure to check [Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP)](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/ship) [enrollment and waiving options](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/insurance/ship-fees-enrollment): All UC Berkeley students are enrolled in SHIP (Student Health Insurance Plan) annually with an option to [waive with their own insurance](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/node/354)if it meets [UC-wide criteria](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/insurance/waiving-ship/ship-waiver-requirements)by January 1, 2026. Note: Be sure to check the [SHIP website](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/insurance/waiving-ship) for the most up-to-date deadlines/fees.
 
## Complete Golden Bear Advising
 
![GBO homepage](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/GBO-HP-300W-300x200.jpg)This is the first step in your Golden Bear Experience. Learn about the online module on our [[Golden Bear Advising - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Advising]] web page; log into CalCentral to access the module.
 
## Complete Golden Bear Prep
 
![Golden Bear Prep](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/golden-bear-prep-386x291-300x226.png)This is the second step in your Golden Bear Experience. Learn about the online module on our [[Golden Bear Prep - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Prep web page]]; log into CalCentral to access the module.
 
## Complete Various Campus Trainings
 
![Sather Gate at sunset](https://live-wp-sa-gbo-1.pantheon.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Houser_DSC_0078-386px-300x200.jpg)UC Berkeley believes in learning and creating an environment that is safe for all. Prior to arriving on campus, you will be given access to two key modules via bCourses: SHAPE and PartySafe at Cal. These courses will provide training on multiple topics including sexual violence prevention, alcohol and other drug education, and equity, diversity and inclusion. The content will help you understand University policies, campus resources, and ways in which you can be an active bystander and community leader by preventing harassment and violence in our community. *Note: additional content/modules that are currently being developed may be added before or after the start of classes.*
 
## Download the Safety App
 
![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Screenshot-2026-03-24-115851.png)
 
Visit the website of the [Office of Emergency Management](https://oem.berkeley.edu/home) for more information on how to stay safe, informed, and prepared. Download the UC Berkeley Safety app to stay informed and receive WarnMe alerts.
 

 
Need help? CSC is here for you.
 
Need a transcript? Have questions about your financial aid or a hold on your registration? [**Cal Student Central**](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/) (not to be confused with CalCentral student portal) is your destination for key university business related to financial aid, fees and billing, payments, disbursements, registration, and enrollment. We offer services online, over the phone, and in person. [Start by using our chat feature or searching our website](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/services-areas-support/) for information and links to additional resources.

## Content

After Golden Bear Orientation, you may participate in Getting Your Bearings, a collection of events sponsored by campus departments and student organizations, for newly admitted undergraduates. It starts the day after Golden Bear Orientation and lasts through the first three weeks of the semester. You may choose from hundreds of events, participating in the ones that mean the most to you.
 
Fall 2026 dates: August 25 – September 13
 
Spring 2027 dates: Check back later for more information
 
Check out the [**Cal Events app**](https://guidebook.com/app/calevents) for events and links in the fall. Although it is not mandatory, Getting Your Bearings offers ways you can shape your experience at Cal, dig deeper into community, and just have fun!

# Golden Bear Advising - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-advising](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-advising)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.644Z

## Content

Golden Bear Advising is [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|mandatory]] and covers campus academic resources and an introduction to your college and includes:
 
- communication with your Academic Adviser 
- an overview of academic resources 
- graduation requirements
 
You’ll be invited through a task in [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/)to complete this online portion of your Golden Bear Experience. Your Golden Bear Advising task on CalCentral is updated manually by your individual college. Please allow up to five business days once you have completed all quizzes, discussions, and/or assignments for your task to be marked as complete. Still see the task as incomplete? Verify that your adviser hasn’t reached out to you for additional information and then contact your college adviser directly, through your Berkeley email or through the Golden Bear Advising module.
 
*Important Note: You must complete Golden Bear Advising in order to connect with your Academic Adviser and to enroll in classes.*
 What you learn in Golden Bear Advising   
- Berkeley Academics OverviewaddIn this portion of your Golden Bear Advising module, you learn about Berkeley's college structure and more about our academic culture, expectations, and opportunities.
- Academic Enrichment & Supportadd
This portion of Golden Bear Advising covers some of our exciting programs, opportunities for enrichment, and support options. For example, you'll learn ways you can thrive in a small academic setting ([Berkeley Connect](http://www.berkeleyconnect.berkeley.edu/)), find undergraduate research opportunities ([Big Ideas](http://bigideas.berkeley.edu/), [undergraduate research](http://research.berkeley.edu/)), or take or teach student-led courses ([DeCal](https://decal.berkeley.edu/)).
- Academic AdvisingaddThis portion of Golden Bear Advising provides unique content from your college or school, including the introduction to your Academic Adviser, an overview of college requirements, basic information on your major or path of study, and directions for selecting your first-semester courses.

## Content

## What to Expect
 
**Overview:** Your Golden Bear Experience consists of four major components:
 
- [[Golden Bear Advising - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Advising]]: Covers campus academic resources, an introduction to your college, and how to enroll in your classes. 
- [[Golden Bear Prep - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Prep]]: Gives you a comprehensive overview of UC Berkeley and your overall transition to campus. 
- [[Golden Bear Orientation Overview - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Orientation (2026-2027)]]: Golden Bear Orientation (GBO) is a program for new undergraduates that helps you: make connections with your peers, faculty, and staff; learn more about available resources and experience campus traditions; broaden your understanding of this diverse and dynamic community; and create a sense of community with your own orientation group and a trained Golden Bear Orientation Leader. 
- [[Getting Your Bearings - Golden Bear Orientation|Getting Your Bearings]]: After Golden Bear Orientation, you may participate in Getting Your Bearings, a collection of events sponsored by campus departments and student organizations, for newly admitted undergraduates. It starts on the first day of classes and lasts through the first three weeks of the semester.
 
**How to Access Advising and Prep:** You access these modules, including start and due dates, through your CalCentral account. *Note: You do not need to register to take these modules (or for any part of the Golden Bear Experience). Simply follow the instructions in CalCentral.*
 
**What’s Required:** You are expected to complete Golden Bear Advising and Golden Bear Prep online, prior to the start of the semester. During Golden Bear Orientation, attending Bear Pact and passing the Bear Pact quiz is ***mandatory*** and students who do not complete these requirements will not be able to enroll in their second semester of courses.

# Golden Bear Orientation Overview - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-orientation](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-orientation)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.645Z

## Content

## About Golden Bear Orientation
 
Golden Bear Orientation is the third phase of the Golden Bear Experience which begins Wednesday, August 19, 2026 and ends Monday, August 24, 2026. We believe there is more to your transition than just registering for classes and taking a tour of campus. GBO reflects the dynamic needs of incoming students and unlike many other institutions, occurs over multiple days immediately before the start of your first semester.
 

 
During GBO, new students are placed in groups with two Orientation Leaders, continuing UC Berkeley students, who guide their group through all kinds of events throughout the four day program. Some example events include community bonding, learning about affinity spaces, becoming familiar with resources on campus, and exploring the Bay Area. In these groups, new students are placed with other students who have a similar incoming status (transfer/first year) and housing experience (I.e., being placed in the same group as those dorming in the same building, those who commute to campus, those living off-campus, etc). This gives students the chance to meet other new incoming students, build connections, and find community. Check out the Fall 2026[[GBO Sample Schedule - Golden Bear Orientation|sample schedule]] to see the variety of programs offered!
 

 
To ensure we are able to serve all students, some of the large-scale components of Golden Bear Orientation will be available to view online after orientation. Golden Bear Advising and Golden Bear Prep have always been online components, and will continue as planned. All of the FAQs below are specific to Fall 2026 Golden Bear Orientation.
 

 
For more information, or if you have concerns about attending GBO, costs, or other housing or financial aid questions, please review our [[FAQS - Golden Bear Orientation|Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)]] and [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|policies.]]

# Golden Bear Prep - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-prep](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/new-students/before-you-arrive/golden-bear-prep)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.644Z

## Content

Golden Bear Prep is [[Policies - Golden Bear Orientation|mandatory]] and gives you a comprehensive overview of UC Berkeley and your overall transition to campus. You’ll be introduced to Berkeley’s traditions, safety, wellness, diversity, and community.
 
This is important because Berkeley offers a vast array of resources, and you gain a huge advantage if you familiarize yourself with them as an incoming student.
 
You’ll be invited through a task in [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) to complete this portion of your Golden Bear Experience. Your Golden Bear Prep task on CalCentral is updated manually. Please allow up to five business days once you have completed all quizzes for your task to be marked as complete.
 What you learn in Golden Bear Prep   
- Berkeley Traditionsadd
Get Berkeley spirit (and bragging rights)! Learn about our traditions, past and present (including the 4.0 Ball and Dead Week), the Free Speech Movement, and all of the aspects that make our culture unique. Go Bears!
- Getting to Know Campus & Bay Areaadd
The Berkeley campus enjoys classic architecture, open green spaces, cutting-edge research facilities, and world-class libraries. You'll want to learn how to get around and, as always, find where the food and coffee spots are.
 
Berkeley's unique location in the Bay Area is a valuable part of your college experience and another reason why you chose to attend this campus. This will help you get acquainted with the world just outside of our campus: San Francisco, Oakland, and the beautiful Bay Area.
- Finding Communityadd
We know you and other incoming students worry about how you will fit in and find your peeps. You start here, by defining what community is and what it means for you at Berkeley. Learn about our standards (Honor Code, Principles of Community, Code of Conduct), where to find help and be a good citizen, and also how to access campus community-building opportunities: [Residential Life](http://reslife.berkeley.edu/), [Transfer Student Resources](http://ce3.berkeley.edu/), [LEAD Center](http://lead.berkeley.edu/), and more. Just know, going in, you belong!
- Diversity & Inclusionadd
Berkeley values diversity for the dynamism and richness it adds to our campus culture. This is where you find out about the spaces we create at Berkeley for diversity and inclusion, including support, resources, and organizations. No matter who you are, which group you identify with, or where you are from, you are welcome.
- Safety & Wellnessadd
Your safety and wellness is of top concern to all of the Berkeley community. Here is where you'll learn all of the aspects around these issues: how to protect yourself, how to find help, how to access Tang Center (university health services) and mental health resources, and how to manage your basic needs (finances, food security, etc.)
- Transition Overviewadd
As you move to campus, settle into your new living space, and prepare to begin the term, you need support. This gives you the help you need to adjust and answer the question: "What should I expect when I come to campus?"
- Countdown to Cal: Student Life Basicsadd
This part of Golden Bear Prep identifies the basics: the student portal CalCentral, managing finances (including [Bears for Financial Success](http://financialaid.berkeley.edu/bears-financial-success) and [personal finance tips](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/financial-literacy-and-resources-financial-literacy-and-resources/learn-tools-tips-and-resources/)), move-in, and the next steps toward the final two steps of your Golden Bear Experience: on campus Golden Bear Orientation and Getting Your Bearings.

# Gracie Hood - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/o-bamgbola](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/o-bamgbola)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.648Z

## Content

[![Gracie Hood, Program Coordinator](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Website-Photos-6.png)](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/about-us/nss-staff/g-hood/) 
Program Coordinator | graciehood@berkeley.edu
 
Gracie joined the New Student Services team in June 2022. Her role oversees Campus Partnership & Student Experience and includes Student Coordinator Recruitment and Supervision, Late Night, and Alumni Mixer. Additionally, she works with Getting Your Bearings and January GBO. Growing up in Birmingham, Alabama, Gracie has spent her college and grad years in North Carolina. She attended the University of North Carolina at Charlotte majoring in International Studies with an undergraduate certificate in Leadership Studies. Her love of being actively involved in college sparked her journey for a M.Ed. in Higher Education Administration from NC State University in Raleigh. Gracie has worked with fraternity & sorority life, student involvement and leadership engagement, multicultural affairs, and advised student government. When she’s not in the office, Gracie can be found eating at cool spots in the city, traveling to new places, and passionately discussing hot takes (i.e. breakfast for dinner gets too much media attention).

### [Perkins and HPSL Loan Entrance Counseling(link is external)](https://www.ecsi.net/promuc1/)
 
Before we can disburse your Federal Perkins or HPSL Loan, regulations require that you complete an entrance counseling session. The counseling session helps guide you in managing your student loan.
          
### [Perkins and HPSL Loan Exit Counseling(link is external)](https://heartland.ecsi.net/)
 
**National Student Loan Database**
 
Exit counseling is required by all students with Perkins or HPSL loans that have graduated, officially withdrawn, dropped below half-time enrollment, transferred to another institution, or simply ceased enrollment at UC Berkeley.
                  
### [Direct Loan Entrance and Exit Counseling(link is external)](https://nslds.ed.gov/nslds/nslds_SA)
 
If you have not previously received Federal student aid, the Federal Government may require you to complete entrance and exit counseling to ensure that you understand your responsibilities and obligations.
          
### [Direct Deposit Enrollment for Students(link is external)](https://eftstudent.berkeley.edu/)
 
Refunds, graduate student stipends, and any non-payroll university payments to students, except Emergency Loan checks, can be directly deposited to your bank account.

# Homepage - Golden Bear Orientation

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.640Z

## Content

Welcome new Golden Bears! Find out what to expect before you arrive. ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png)     Golden Bear Orientation See sample schedules to get an idea of what to expect for your orientation experience and learn about our programs. ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png) ![decorative image](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/plugins/revslider/sr6/assets/assets/dummy.png)   WelcomeGolden Bear Orientation      
A warm welcome to UC Berkeley. New Student Services’ mission is to give each student the support and resources needed for a successful transition to the Berkeley campus: academically, socially, emotionally, and culturally. Here you’ll find a guide through the overall *Golden Bear Experience*, which consists of four major components: *Golden Bear Advising, Golden Bear Prep, Golden Bear Orientation and Getting Your Bearings.*
 
Whether you are an incoming undergraduate first-year or a transfer student, please take the time to read through the information here. Your transition to Berkeley begins online as soon as you accept your offer of admission! Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us. Our staff is here to answer your questions and offer advice. Welcome to Cal and Go Bears!
                    
- ![Golden Bear Advising](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/20180815_GBO_bhs_030_hp_1stbox_400x300.jpg)   [[Golden Bear Advising - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Advising]] Step 1: Complete Advising online for academics and enrollment. 
- ![Golden Bear Prep](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/20180816_GBO_bhs_002_hp_2ndbox_400x300.jpg)   [[Golden Bear Prep - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Prep]] Step 2: Take Prep online to learn Berkeley's history, find community, and explore the culture. 
- ![Golden Bear Orientation](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/20180815_GBO_bhs_080_hp_3rdbox_400x300.jpg)   [[Golden Bear Orientation Overview - Golden Bear Orientation|Golden Bear Orientation]] Step 3: This program will help you find resources and make connections.

- **Source URL**: [https://orientation.berkeley.edu/how-to-get-involved](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/how-to-get-involved)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-09T06:43:01.643Z

## Content

![People setting up booths for GBO](https://orientation.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/DSC_7199_775x401.jpg)
 
We’d love you to be involved with Golden Bear Orientation!
 
Share your passion for Cal with our newly admitted students and welcome the latest generation of Golden Bears to UC Berkeley.
 
We have opportunities in a wide variety of areas, including:
 
- Orientation Leaders : Help guide students through a multi-day orientation program to help prepare them for success at UC Berkeley. 
- Orientation Mentors : Mentor a group of Orientation Leaders as well as training them in leadership development. 
- Student Coordinators: Serve as role models to Mentors, Leaders, and all the new students. 
- Office Representatives: Provide quality customer service to incoming students who contact NSS with questions and concerns. 
- Faculty/Staff Volunteers: Sign up for any one of a number of opportunities, including welcoming new students or visitors, helping with logistics, and assisting at Convocation.
