# How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/how-to-enroll-in-classes/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/how-to-enroll-in-classes/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.774Z

## Content

**On this page (click link to jump to section):**
 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Plan Your Schedule]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Course Loads]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|How to Use the Class Schedule]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Search by Major Requirements]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Enroll in Courses in CalCentral]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Schedule Planner]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Undergraduate Add-drop Deadlines]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Late Add-Drop Fees]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Details About Adds, Drops, and Waitlists]] 
- [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|Enrollment Questions]]
 
## Plan Your Schedule
 
Before you enroll in classes, use these resources to plan your schedule.
 
- Go to the [Class Schedule](http://classes.berkeley.edu/) and use the search and filters to find amazing classes for the term you are planning. 
- Visit [X.com/BerkeleyGuide](http://x.com/BerkeleyGuide) to see Suggested Classes with open seats. Follow [@BerkeleyGuide](http://x.com/BerkeleyGuide) on X to see open classes as they are recommended by departments and faculty. 
- Plan your schedule within [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/). 
- Set up a meeting with your adviser at your college and/or department to enroll.
 
### Course Loads
 
Students are expected to maintain a normal course load each semester. Reduced course loads must be approved.
 
- Undergraduate students: A course load of 15 units per semester is considered a normal undergraduate course load. You are generally expected to enroll in at least 15 units. Some colleges have a minimum course load requirement of 12 or 13 units. Visit the [[Registration and Payment - Office of the Registrar|Registration and Payment]] page for more information about unit requirements. 
- Graduate students: A course load of 12 units per semester is considered a normal, full-time graduate course load.
       
- Reduced course loads must be approved by the dean's office of your college or school. If you are an undergraduate and anticipate being enrolled in fewer than the minimum number of units required by your college or school, contact your dean's office as soon as possible to request approval to be enrolled in a less-than-full course load. Requests should be submitted before the end of the previous semester to have time for review. A reduced course load must be approved by the dean of your college or school before the end of your Phase II enrollment period.
 
## How to Use the Class Schedule
 
The [Class Schedule](https://classes.berkeley.edu/) is a robust tool supported by the Office of the Registrar to help you explore Berkeley’s offerings and find amazing classes that fit your needs. There are many ways to customize, filter, and layer your search for classes.
 
These search features in the Class Schedule can help you find courses that meet your needs:
 
- View an alphanumeric list of classes by Department Subject from the secondary drop-down menu. 
- Layer on your selected term for your search and use keywords. 
- Search by days offered or start time. 
- Explore all classes that satisfy the Historical Studies Breadth requirement and the American Cultures requirement. 
- Find a class by instructor or ones that still have open seats. 
- Search the Major Requirements feature based on your entry year (details below).
 
### Search by Major Requirements
 
The [Class Schedule](https://classes.berkeley.edu/) allows students to search for classes in a given term that fulfill specific major requirements. This search feature is brought to you by the Student Technology Fund (STF). To search by Major Requirements, select filters for:
 
- **Requirement year |** In the left-hand toolbar, find the dropdown for Major Requirements and select your requirement year. Generally, the requirement year is when you were admitted to Berkeley or your major.* 
- **Major |** After selecting a requirement year, a second drop-down menu will appear under Major Requirements. Select your declared or intended major from the list. 
- **Term |** At the top of the left-hand toolbar, select the term in which you would like to search for classes. The search is possible from Spring 2020 class offerings to present.
 
Use the left-hand column filters to narrow your search to specific requirements, classes with open seats, classes at certain times, classes that fulfill breadth requirements, etc.
 
*Declared students can verify their requirement year in CalCentral’s [Academic Progress Report](https://sis.berkeley.edu/generate-academic-progress-report-apr) (APR).
 ![Academic Objective summary showing an undergraduate Data Science BA student with an expected graduation term of Fall 2019.](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/Academic-Objective.png)
In CalCentral, the Academic Progress Report will include the Academic Objective. This image shows an academic objective summary for an undergraduate student in the College of Letters & Science at UC Berkeley. The student is pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Data Science with a subplan in Applied Mathematics & Modeling. Their catalog term for the program is Fall 2016, while the major and subplan were declared in Fall 2018. The expected graduation term is Fall 2019, and the graduation status indicates eligibility for graduation.
 
Learn how to use the Major Requirements search feature in the Class Schedule by watching this video.
        
- The search feature was released in October 2019 with a nine-major pilot that has since expanded to 18 majors in total. These majors account for nearly 50% of all declared students. The Search by Major Requirements feature will expand each semester to include more majors and provide undergraduates with a unique tool for exploring the classes they need to complete their degrees.
 
See the [Class Schedule FAQs](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vRtUZxfjNYlNVnGGlc1L2iYnZtrbxOfKhp1IYVozhh3ywfIWnOuD0kgGb7_4jtdn0rpZEC9l-0Xk9aF/pub) for answers to additional questions including:
 
- Where information from the Class Schedule is sourced 
- How long it takes the Class Schedule to display data
 
## Enroll in Courses in CalCentral
 
Enrollment occurs in CalCentral. You choose classes, add them to a shopping cart, and then enroll. The shopping cart allows you to select classes before your enrollment appointment time so that you are ready to enroll when it is time.
 
### Schedule Planner
 
The Schedule Planner in CalCentral allows you to input your intended courses and see how they would fit together in a weekly schedule. You can add classes directly to your shopping cart with the planner.
 
### Undergraduate Add-drop Deadlines
 
You add or drop classes within CalCentral. The [Student Calendar](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/calendars/) includes dates you can add/drop (and when the add/drop fee applies).
 
**Classes must be added or dropped by 11:59 p.m. (Pacific time) on Wednesday of week four of the semester.**
 
- Early Drop Deadline (EDD) classes can be dropped only through the Friday of week two of the semester. 
- The Fall Program for First Semester (FPF) add-drop deadline is the fourth Wednesday of the Fall semester. 
- The deadline to change units for variable unit classes is the Wednesday of week four of the semester (same as the add-drop deadline). 
- The concurrent-enrollment deadline to *add* classes is Wednesday of week four of the semester. 
- The concurrent enrollment deadline to *drop* classes is Friday of week four of the semester.
 
*The drop deadline does not impact financial aid policies. Satisfactory Academic Progress is evaluated based on the number of units you are enrolled in at the end of week five. Financial aid will continue to evaluate your eligibility for Federal Pell Grant and/or Cal Grant based on your enrollment on the Friday of week five. If you are enrolled in less than 12 units at that time, your awards may be adjusted.*
 
### Late Add/Drop Fees
 
- Students will be charged a $10 late fee for each class dropped after the end of the second Friday of instruction (11:59 p.m. PST). 
- Students will be charged a $5 fee for each class added after the end of the third week of instruction (11:59 p.m. PST on Friday).
 
Note: If you are not officially registered by the end of the third week of instruction, you’ll be charged a $150 late-registration fee* when you become officially registered (view [[Registration and Payment - Office of the Registrar|Registration and Payment]] for a full definition of official registration, which means: being enrolled in at least one class, having no blocks on your CalCentral account, and paying at least 20% tuition and fees).
 
*This late-registration fee is currently suspended.
 
### Details About Adds, Drops, and Waitlists
       
- If you want to enroll in (add) a class, keep in mind:
 
- Departments may reserve seats in classes for students who meet certain criteria, based on major, level, etc. These classes are indicated in the [Berkeley Guide Class Schedule](http://classes.berkeley.edu/) and CalCentral. 
- If you qualify for a seat reservation category but it is full, you will receive the message: "The enrollment category for which you qualify is full." 
- If you attempt to add a course and you do not meet the restrictions, you will not be allowed to enroll, and you will receive the message, "You have not met the enrollment restrictions (or criteria) for this class," or "Students at your course level are not permitted to enroll in this class."
 
Visit this site for [Enrollment FAQs](https://sis.berkeley.edu/help/enrollment-faq).
- If you attempt to enroll in classes with overlapping days/times, you will only be able to do so if at least one of the conflicting classes is set up to allow time overlaps with other classes. You must click YES after you receive the error message “A scheduling conflict exists, please press 'yes' to accept and continue."
 If both conflicting classes are not set up for students to enroll in classes with time conflicts, you will be unable to enroll in both classes while the times conflict. You must choose one or the other or find alternatives that allow time conflicts or do not conflict.
- To drop an enrolled or waitlisted class, go to your current class schedule and select the class you wish to drop. You must confirm the transaction before the class will be dropped from your schedule. Please be aware some courses have [early drop deadlines (EDD)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vSqiDFBNz3PrnrWDSTnacfQ4EKwOl1f3rsaZxO7mdSuIf8S2CD7PS86uHqzNShU_Cq-IfSk4NMxUSrz/pub). Check your college/school's website for more information.
 
Students are allowed to drop below full-time units until the end of the fourth week of instruction. Students will be charged a $10 late fee for each class dropped after the end of the second Friday of instruction.
 
**If you do not plan to attend/enroll for the semester**, you will not be able to drop your last class. You must submit a withdrawal form on CalCentral > My Dashboard > Student Resources > eForms Center > Submit an eForm > Term Cancel/Withdraw Request.
- If you are not enrolled in any classes by the deadline (below), you will need approval to enroll in any class.
 
**Undergraduate Enrollment Deadline**
 
If you are an undergraduate student and you have not enrolled in classes by the end of the fourth Wednesday of instruction (11:59 p.m. PST), you must obtain approval from an adviser in your college or school in order to enroll.
 
**Graduates Enrollment Deadline**
 
If you are a graduate student and you have not enrolled in classes by the end of the fifth Friday of instruction (11:59 p.m. PST), you must reach out to your Graduate Student Affairs Officer (GSAO) to submit a re-enrollment request on your behalf.
 
Each school or college has its own policies and procedures regarding student requests for exceptions to add or drop a class after the add/drop deadline. Please see your college adviser if you have questions.
 
Add and drop deadlines are set by the colleges and approved by the Council of Undergraduate Deans, the body where the undergraduate colleges convene to make collective decisions. All of the undergraduate colleges have a stake in consistent deadlines, because students from every college take courses in every other college.
- If you are unable to enroll in a class because it is full, there are two ways you may be added to a waitlist: automatic or manual. You can find the waitlist options in CalCentral.
 
**1) Automatic.** You can place yourself on the class's waitlist in CalCentral. Automatic wait lists are processed every three hours through the end of the third week of instruction. Students on automatic waitlists are enrolled sequentially, provided there are seats available for their enrollment group.
 
Note: If you are already enrolled in a class that conflicts with the scheduling of a class you are waitlisted for, it is considered a time conflict. You will not be automatically enrolled from a wait list if there is a time conflict in your schedule and both classes do not allow time conflicts.
 
**2) Manual.** An instructor or department can change a waitlist from automatic to manual (or vice versa) at any time. An instructor/department also can selectively choose to add students from a waitlist and may not adhere to the sequential order of students on the waitlist. (Students added this way are not charged a $5 add fee.) Departments may enroll students from a manual waitlist beginning the first day of Phase I through the end of the fourth week of instruction.
 
Waitlisted students usually receive first priority for enrollment. However, there is no guarantee that you will be enrolled in the course. Being enrolled from a wait list depends on a number of factors, such as whether the list is "automatic" or "manual," your position on the list, the size of the course, and whether enough space becomes available (through drops or an increase in seats).
 
Units for waitlisted courses are counted as part of your unit total. You need to be actually enrolled (i.e., not on the waitlist) in at least one course to be considered officially "registered" (in addition to having paid at least 20 percent of your registration fees and having no registration holds).
- If you are waitlisted for a class, be proactive about committing to or dropping the class. Waitlisted students who want to get into the class will want to check in with the instructor or GSI to see if they want waitlisted students to attend or not, and if they do, then definitely attend and keep up on the work.
 If you no longer wish to take a waitlisted course, you are responsible for dropping yourself from the waitlist, preferably by the end of the second week of instruction.
 
- Be sure to drop yourself from the waitlist before the add-drop deadline. 
- If you have already been enrolled from a waitlist, you are responsible for dropping the class. 
- Enrollment managers add students from waitlists on Thursday and Friday of week four of the semester. If you are added into a class on these days it will be too late to drop it.
- Be sure to do all the homework. If you are having trouble with homework or understanding lectures and class concepts, try attending office hours. If you continue to have trouble with material even after discussing it with your professor or graduate student instructor, this could be an indication that the class is not right for you.
- You should always drop any unwanted classes from your schedule immediately. Don't wait for or assume an instructor will drop you from a class.
 
However, an instructor may drop you from a class if you do not attend every class meeting during the first three weeks of instruction or if you do not meet the prerequisites.
- As of January 2020, the policy for auditing classes has changed. Please see the complete [Policy for Auditing Classes at UC Berkeley (PDF)](http://evcp.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/policy_for_auditing_classes_at_uc_berkeley.pdf) for details.
 
## Enrollment Questions
 
Students, if you have technical questions about enrollment procedures (add/drop, waitlist, swap, etc.) in Cal Student Central, please contact [Cal Student Central](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/services-areas-support/) (CSC) for support.
 
- We recommend reviewing this [Enrollment FAQ](https://sis.berkeley.edu/help/enrollment-faq) before contacting CSC as it may address your questions. 
- For any course-related questions, please contact the department offering the course.
 
Academic departments, if you have any questions about the content displayed in the [Class Schedule](https://classes.berkeley.edu/), please email [class-schedule@berkeley.edu](mailto:class-schedule@berkeley.edu).

# Notary Services - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/notary-services/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/notary-services/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.778Z

## Content

We can notarize the following UC Berkeley documents: official transcripts, verification documents, and diplomas or diploma photocopies.
 
## Get a UC Berkeley Transcript, Verification, or Diploma Notarized
 
The processing fee for this service is $15 per document. We make arrangements to have documents notarized twice a month, usually during the first and third week of each month. For diplomas, you must provide a photocopy to notarize.
 
**Notarization with CalCentral Access**
 
Current students, alumni and former students with access may request Notary Services on [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) > My Dashboard > Student Resources > eForms Center > Submit an eForm > Custom Verification Request > Select Attend and Degrees
 
**Notarization without CalCentral Access**
 
Students and alumni who no longer have access to CalCentral may request Notary Services by completing a [Request for Verification of Attendance and Degrees Form (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/Verification_Request_Form.pdf) and submitting it in one of the following ways:
 
- Bring the form in person to Cal Student Central, 120 Sproul Hall. 
- Mail the form to the Office of the Registrar address on our [About](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/about) page. 
- Email the form to [Verify-Attendance-Degrees@berkeley.edu](mailto:Verify-Attendance-Degrees@berkeley.edu).
 
**Apostilles**
 
Apostilles are available exclusively from the California Secretary of State. They certify the authenticity of signatures by California Notaries Public. If you need an Apostille for a document notarized by the Office of the Registrar, please visit the [California Secretary of State](http://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/authentication/) for information and instruction.
 
An Apostille is likely *not necessary* for students eligible for the certified electronic diploma (beginning with Spring 2020 graduates). See the [Credential Validation](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/credential-validation) page for more information.

# Official Transcripts - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/official-transcripts/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/official-transcripts/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.776Z

## Content

Degrees are posted on a student’s official transcript approximately three months after the end of the term.
 
*Please note: Degree completion is contingent on all grades for all semesters being posted to the transcripts.*
 
## Ordering or Requesting a Transcript
 
Read the sections below for information about ordering transcripts. Please note there is a specialized transcript request process for the following:
 
- Berkeley Law students and alumni may order transcripts directly from the [Law School Registrar](https://www.law.berkeley.edu/academics/registrar/transcripts/). 
- UC Berkeley Extension students and alumni may order transcripts from [UC Berkeley Extension](https://extension.berkeley.edu/static/studentservices/transcripts/) directly.
       
- **Current Students**
 
Current students may order transcripts online through our student portal, [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/), or they may order paper copies on the spot at Cal Student Central in 120 Sproul Hall.
 
Berkeley can now send fully electronic transcripts (EDI) to receiving institutions. This is the fastest and most secure method. Effective January 1, 2020, transcripts are no longer withheld if a student has a Financial Hold.
 
**Parchment Support**
 
If you have problems with an electronic transcript order, you can contact Parchment Support by phone at 888-662-0874 or by [submitting a ticket](https://parchment.my.site.com/admin/s/contactsupport) at parchment.my.site.com/admin/s/contactsupport.
 
**Alumni and Summer Visitors**
 
Alumni and summer sessions visitors may order transcripts using [Parchment](https://www.parchment.com/u/registration/32361/institution).
 
**Berkeley Law Alumni**
 
Alumni of Berkeley Law should visit the [Berkeley Law](https://www.law.berkeley.edu/academics/registrar/transcripts/) website for information on ordering a transcript.
- **Current Students**
 
Current students may send a transcript to an application processing service such as AMCAS (American Medical College Application Service), LSDAS (Law School Data Assembly Service), PHARMCAS (Pharmacy College Application Service), other processing services, or order through [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
 
**Alumni and Summer Visitors**
 
Alumni and Summer Sessions visitors may order transcripts using [Parchment](https://www.parchment.com/u/registration/32361/institution).
 
**Note:** The UC Berkeley transcript order forms (for current students and alumni) include a field to add the unique identifier for your application. Therefore, you do not need to include additional forms to be "attached" with your order.
- If you attended during Fall Semester or Spring Semester, a transcript will be forwarded to your home campus approximately **five to six weeks after** the term has ended. Your coursework and grades will be included in your home-campus record. If a change occurs after the work is transferred, a replacement transcript will be sent to the home campus.
 
## Managing Your Transcript
 
**Your Name on Records**
 
For information about how your name appears on records and rosters, or for details about how to change the way your name appears, visit [Update Name & Personal Information](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/student-records/update-name-personal-information/).
 
**Notary Services**
 
UC Berkeley can notarize your official transcripts. For information, visit [Notary Services](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/student-records/notary-services/).
 
**Graduate with Money Owed to the University**
 
Effective Spring 2018, students who owe money to the university will be able to graduate, but their [diplomas](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/student-records/diplomas/) will be withheld. Once a student makes their payment and the system is updated, the student will be emailed to verify their mailing address for the diploma.
 
## Proof of Graduation Before Degrees Are Posted
 
### Undergraduate Students
 
Degrees are posted on the official transcript approximately three months after the end of the term.
 
**Diplomas are not available until approximately 4 months after the end of term.**
 
In a small number of cases, individuals who demonstrate an urgent need for proof of conferral may request an expedited degree posting. Since several offices must review the candidate’s academic record, these requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis. All grades for all semesters must be posted to be considered for an expedited degree. After all your grades are posted **and** you have submitted your request for an expedited degree, please allow three to five weeks of review time.
 
If you need to prove you graduated after the degree is posted, request a transcript or [education and degree verification](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/student-records/education-degree-verification/).
 
**Registered Undergraduate Students**
 
Degree completion is contingent on **all grades for all semesters being posted to the transcripts**. Degree posting to transcripts begins after the end of each semester (for Summer, after all sessions end), depending on grades and college review and approval. Individuals who demonstrate an urgent need for proof of conferral may request an [expedited degree](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfYpfysuHA_lLLAnoiKXI06b32Y7VmRznOZ1VLPCal0AKYAaA/viewform?usp=header). Requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis. **Note:** You must be logged into your official Berkeley email in order to access the request form.
       
- **For questions about the expedited process, contact the appropriate staff listed below.**
 
If you are graduating from:
 
- College of Letters & Science (Last name A–F) 
- College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (Last name A–F) 
- College of Engineering 
- Rausser College of Natural Resources 
- **Contact Vanessa Robbins ([vanessar@berkeley.edu](mailto:vanessar@berkeley.edu))**
 
If you are graduating from:
 
- College of Letters & Science (Last name G–N) 
- College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (Last name G–N) 
- College of Chemistry 
- School of Education 
- **Contact Paige Corey ([pcorey@berkeley.edu](mailto:pcorey@berkeley.edu))**
 
If you are graduating from:
 
- College of Letters & Science (Last name O–Z) 
- College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (Last name O–Z) 
- Haas School of Business 
- College of Environmental Design 
- **Contact Grace Padua ([gspadua@berkeley.edu](mailto:gspadua@berkeley.edu))**
- Non-enrolled students who need proof of graduation (**before the end of the term of graduation**) can submit a request for a [Certificate of Completion](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdZBuNjdWE6SS_d1flDwMq3OO3COJt9oPXhQp-RhGytd2ye_g/viewform). Requests will be reviewed and processed only after the end of the add/drop period for the semester of graduation **and** before the end of the term of graduation.
 
**If you submit a request for a Certificate of Completion after your graduation term is over, your request will not be processed** because the Office of the Registrar is already posting degrees at that point.
 
*All graduation requirements must be fulfilled for this certificate to be released.* Please allow our staff up to 10 business days to complete your request and mail the paper certificate to you.
 
### Graduate Students
 
When all requirements are satisfied in the system, Certificates of Completion are automatically generated and emailed to graduate students.
 
## Special Order Requests
       
- If family members are living, they must order the transcript for themselves using [Parchment](https://www.parchment.com/u/registration/32361/institution).
 
If the family member is deceased, you may order the transcript by including a death certificate or obituary along with the order. Please write a letter and include the following:
 
- Name 
- Birth date 
- Dates of attendance 
- Field of study (if known)
 
You can send us the letter via physical mail to: Transcripts, Office of the Registrar, 128 Sproul Hall, University of California, Berkeley, CA 94720-5404, or email us at [transcripts@berkeley.edu](mailto:transcripts@berkeley.edu). The transcripts will be sent via first-class mail and could take up to 30 days to arrive. There is no fee for this service.

# Readmission - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/readmission/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/readmission/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.775Z

## Content

If you were an [[Glossary - Office of the Registrar|enrolled]] student pursuing a UC Berkeley degree at any point and would like to return, you need to be readmitted or approved for re-enrollment.
 
## Considerations for Readmission
 
Readmission and re-enrollment is not guaranteed. The decision ultimately rests with your college, school, or the Graduate Division, each of which has different expectations, deadlines, and requirements. Please consult your college, school, or the Graduate Division for detailed information.
 
- **Undergraduate students** who left the University and were absent for one or more semesters must apply for readmission. 
- **Graduate students** who were absent from the University for one or more semesters or were on Filing Fee status but did not file their dissertation must apply for re-enrollment.
 
All academic, administrative, and [registration holds](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/registration-academic-records/registration-enrollment/) (all holds except those placed by Financial Aid) must be cleared from your account before your request for readmission/re-enrollment will be processed.
 
*Note: Your college, school, or the Graduate Division may take weeks to adjudicate your application. The Office of the Registrar processes approved applications within 3–5 business days after receipt from the colleges, schools, and Graduate Division.*
 
Students interested in applying for financial aid can prepare in advance by reviewing the [eligibility](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/how-aid-works/eligibility/) page, the [Financial Aid Checklist](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/how-aid-works/financial-aid-checklist/) page, and the [Estimate Your Aid](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/how-aid-works/estimate-your-financial-aid/) page.
 
**International students:** If you are an F-1/J-1 visa International Student seeking entry to the U.S. after your readmission has been processed by the Office of the Registrar, please access the [Non-Immigrant Information (NIF)](https://internationaloffice.berkeley.edu/students/nif) task in your CalCentral dashboard to request an I-20/DS-2019. If you have questions or concerns, please [contact the Berkeley International Office](https://internationaloffice.berkeley.edu/contact-us) for assistance.
 
### When to Apply for Readmission
 
For undergraduates, the deadlines for the readmission application are:
 
- June 1 for the Fall Semester 
- November 1 for the Spring Semester
 
Graduate students should consult the [Academic Calendar](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/calendars/academic-calendar/) for registration information and deadlines.
 
### Applying for Readmission After a Medical Withdrawal
 
Students returning after a Medical Withdrawal should consult [University Health Services](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/counseling/social-services/academic-adjustments-and-medical-withdrawals), which will process approval of a Health Clearance for Readmission Application form. This process may take up to thirty days and is required to be completed before the Office of the Registrar can act upon an Application for Readmission.
 
## Apply for Readmission as an Undergraduate
 
For your college or school to adjudicate your application for readmission, you must complete the steps outlined below.
 
**Step 1 | Clear all [Registration Holds](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/registration-academic-records/registration-enrollment/).**
 
- Applications cannot be evaluated until all holds are cleared (except those from Financial Aid and Student Conduct). 
- This includes a health clearance by [University Health Services](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/counseling/social-services/academic-adjustments-and-medical-withdrawals) (UHS), which is required before those granted a medical withdrawal approved by UHS may be readmitted. 
- EOP students with a past due balance hold are strongly encouraged to apply to the [EOP Readmission Equity Grant](https://eop.berkeley.edu/readmission-equity-grant) for financial assistance and holistic academic counseling support.
 
**Step 2 | Complete the [Undergraduate Application for Readmission (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/readmission_form.pdf).** Indicate your current major program or undeclared status. If you wish to change or declare your major program:
 
- - College of Letters and Science students should follow the [L&S readmission guidelines](https://lsadvising.berkeley.edu/policies/readmission). 
- Rausser College of Natural Resources students should follow the [RCNR Readmission Policies and Procedures](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Su7g7nJk8KFgEID8yCGcOez8u7_j3IrEY2ZjsLSEQw/edit?tab=t.u0esrlkfya8#heading=h.2rjoqym4gs8l).
 
- All other students should complete the [Undergraduate Petition Change of College, Major or Curriculum (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/col.maj_.ug_a11y.pdf) and follow the submission instructions.
 
**Step 3 | Pay the Readmission Fee.** After the college has approved the readmission, pay the $70 Readmission Application Fee,* which is non-refundable and non-transferable. Please note: If you send your payment before obtaining approval from the college, we cannot accept it. We accept payment via:
 
- Check or money order payable to UC Regents 
- Credit or Debit card paid online (instructions will be sent via email)
 
**The [Educational Opportunity Program (EOP)](http://www.eop.berkeley.edu/) offers a fee waiver to cover the $70 readmission application cost. To request the EOP Readmission Fee waiver, [please complete the fee waiver request form here](https://docs.google.com/forms/u/1/d/e/1FAIpQLSepmj0YKoRuECHvJUUv9bmuf9JxciQ5JajECdDy_zjcS2xbKg/viewform?usp=send_form) and [schedule to meet with an EOP Counselor](https://eop.berkeley.edu/services-programs/schedule-appointment). Please email [eop@berkeley.edu](mailto:eop@berkeley.edu) for additional questions.*
 
**Step 4 | Submit transcripts of any outside coursework.** Enclose official transcripts of all coursework taken at another institution—including UC Berkeley Extension—during your absence. Official transcripts may be submitted separately from your application and payment.
 
**Step 5 | Submit your readmission materials.** Send materials directly to your college or school advising office:
 
- [College of Chemistry](https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/ugrad/current-students/withdrawal) 
- [College of Engineering](https://engineering.berkeley.edu/students/undergraduate-guide/policies-procedures/withdrawal/#ac12277) 
- [College of Environmental Design](https://ced.berkeley.edu/students/undergraduate-advising/policies-resources) 
- [College of Letters and Science](https://ls.berkeley.edu/ls-office-undergraduate-advising) 
- [Rausser College of Natural Resources](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Su7g7nJk8KFgEID8yCGcOez8u7_j3IrEY2ZjsLSEQw/edit?tab=t.u0esrlkfya8) 
- [Haas School of Business](https://haas.berkeley.edu/undergrad/academics/advising/) 
- [College of Computing, Data Science, and Society](https://cdss.berkeley.edu/academics/policies) 
- [Berkeley School of Education](https://bse.berkeley.edu/academics/undergraduate-programs/policies/student-status-changes)
 
**Important Notes:**
 
- Upon readmission, you must submit an online Statement of Legal Residence at [Cal Student Central](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/) (calcentral.berkeley.edu). 
- Your college or school may take weeks to adjudicate your application. 
- The Office of the Registrar will process your readmission within 3–5 business after receipt of **both** the approved application from your college or school and your payment of the $70 application fee.
 
## Apply for Readmission to a Graduate Program
 
Graduate students absent from the University for one or more semesters or on Filing Fee status but did not file their dissertation should consult the [Graduate Division Readmission and Re-enrollment](http://grad.berkeley.edu/policy/registration-and-exchange-programs-policy/#d19-readmission-and-re-enrollment) policies and procedures. If you qualify for re-enrollment based on these policies, you must:
 
- Clear all academic, administrative, and [registration holds](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/registration-academic-records/registration-enrollment/) (all holds except those from Financial Aid). 
- Contact your Head Graduate Adviser for assistance with the re-enrollment process and to have a re-enrollment request submitted to the Office of the Registrar on your behalf. 
- Check CalCentral for follow-up items you must complete, such as submitting an online Statement of Legal Residence (SLR)* and updating your contact information in [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/).
 
Submit all required documents to your Program Office. Your Graduate Student Affairs Officer (GSAO) will notify you once you are eligible for re-enrollment. The Office of the Registrar processes approved applications within 3–5 business days after receipt from the Graduate Division.
 
**Some professional programs are exempt from a residence determination. If you are uncertain if yours is among them, please consult your Program Office.*

# Refunds After Withdrawal - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/cancellation-withdrawal/refunds-after-withdrawal/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/cancellation-withdrawal/refunds-after-withdrawal/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.775Z

## Content

**The percentage of refunds depends on the effective date of your withdrawal.**
 
Fee adjustments, if any, are based on your withdrawal date. All fee adjustments for withdrawals are applied to your student account and may be applied to any outstanding debts. If you are participating in the Deferred Payment Plan and have not paid all your fees, you may still owe fees to the University. Please see the tables below for prorated amounts **based on calendar days (including weekends and holidays)** beginning on the first day of instruction (according to the [Academic Calendar](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/calendars/academic-calendar/)).
 
The following fees are nonrefundable as of the first day of instruction:
 
- Late fees 
- Health Insurance 
- Transit Fee (formerly known as Class Pass Transit Fee) 
- Document Management Fee
 
## Fee Adjustments
 
Calendar days are based on the first date of instruction for each term.
 
- Undergraduate, Academic, and Professional Graduate students, please review the [Academic Calendar](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/calendars/academic-calendar/) for the first date of instruction for each term. 
- For law students and students in self-supporting graduate professional degree programs, please check with your program office.
 
Note: Tuition and mandatory fees have been set regardless of the method of instruction and will not be refunded in the event instruction occurs remotely for any part of the Academic Year.
 
## Before Federal Financial Aid Has Been Applied
 
All continuing, readmitted students, and new students who have not had federal Title IV financial aid applied to their accounts:
     Calendar Days Prorated Fees   Before instruction begins 0%   First Day of Instruction 0%   2-11 10%   12-27 50%   28-53 75%   54+ 100%     
## After Federal Financial Aid Has Been Applied (New Students)
 
New students who have had federal Title IV financial aid applied to their accounts who withdraw during their first term of enrollment:
     **Calendar Days** **Prorated Fees**   Before instruction begins 0%   1-7 0%   8-14 10%   15-28 20%   29-35 30%   36-49 40%   50-56 50%   57-63 60%   64+ 100%     
## Financial Aid Recipients
 
If you are a financial aid recipient and withdraw, you may have to pay back all or part of your financial aid, as you may no longer be eligible for the full amount of aid. If you are still in student housing, you will be held responsible for all Housing and Dining charges before the first day of courses and after your effective withdrawal date.
 
These charges will not be part of financial aid eligibility, nor will they be subject to refund. Financial aid will not be provided to cover any of these charges. Please consult with the Financial Aid and Scholarship office at [withdraw@berkeley.edu](mailto:withdraw@berkeley.edu) and include your Student ID Number.

# Registration and Payment - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/registration-and-payment/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/registration-and-payment/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.774Z

## Content

Registration confirms your status as a student at UC Berkeley. Registering at Berkeley consists of two steps:
 
- Enrolling in classes. 
- Paying your bill.*
 
***Important note for students:** You must pay at least 20% of your bill by the Friday before instruction begins.
 
## Official Registration
 
To be officially registered at UC Berkeley, you must meet these three criteria by the deadline each semester (the Friday before instruction begins).
 
- **You must be enrolled in at least one class.** By the third week of instruction, you are also expected to be enrolled in at least the minimum number of units approved by your college or school. Minimum requirements vary but are typically 12 or more units. 
- **20% of tuition and fees must be paid (even if not yet due).** This percentage is the first installment amount of the [Fee Payment Plan](http://studentbilling.berkeley.edu/deferredPay.htm). 
- View your bill within the [My Finances section of CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/finances). 
- Students who cannot pay will be dropped from their courses and are subject to the [Cancel for Non-Payment Policy](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/registration/cancellation-withdrawal/cancel-for-non-payment-policy/). *This policy is on hold until further notice; please visit the web page for details.* 
- If you need assistance, access our [[Support for Staying Enrolled - Office of the Registrar|Support for Staying Enrolled]], which includes financial support options and other resources. 
- **You must not have holds against your registration.** Log in to CalCentral to find out if you have any holds, and if so, follow the instructions on clearing them. View the hold details and instructions in CalCentral > My Academics > Status and Holds section. The type of registration hold (financial, academic, or administrative) will determine what action needs to be taken to resolve it. (For details, navigate to “Registration Holds” at [Cal Student Central Registration & Enrollment](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/registration-academic-records/registration-enrollment/).)
 
To be eligible to enroll in the next term, you must be officially registered on CalCentral for the current term. Once you are officially registered, you can access campus services for students, such as library privileges, the Recreational Sports Facility, University Health Services, etc.
 
**Registration Deadline**
 
If you are not officially registered by the end of the third week of instruction, you may lose access to various campus services (University Health Services, Recreation Sports Facility, bConnected software, etc.). Additionally you will be charged a $150 late-registration fee (this fee will not be assessed during the 2025–26 academic year and is suspended until further notice). Be sure to officially register by the deadline.
 
### Minimum Unit Requirements
 
You must be enrolled in at least one class to be considered a registered student at Berkeley. However, you are expected to be enrolled in at least the minimum number of units approved by your college or school by the end of the third week of instruction. Minimum unit requirements are as follows.
 
**Undergraduate Minimum Unit Requirements**
 
- Haas School of Business: 13 Units 
- College of Chemistry: 13 Units 
- College of Engineering: 12 Units 
- College of Environmental Design: 12 Units 
- College of Letters & Science: 13 Units 
- Rausser College of Natural Resources: 12 Units 
- College of Computing, Data Science, and Society: 12 Units
 
**Graduate Minimum Unit Requirements**
 
- All graduate students: 12 Units 
- Graduate students under special programs, such as fellowships or certain financial aid, have different minimum unit requirements. Consult your department.
 
### Maximum Unit Enrollment
 
While you are expected to be enrolled in at least the minimum unit requirements, there are limits on maximum units as well.
 
**Undergraduate Maximum Unit Limits**
 
- Haas School of Business: 20.5 Units 
- College of Chemistry: 20.5 Units 
- College of Engineering: 20.5 Units 
- College of Environmental Design: 20.5 Units 
- College of Letters & Science: 20.5 Units 
- College of Natural Resources: 20.5 Units
 
**Graduate Maximum Unit Limits**
 
- Law School students: 16.0 Units 
- All other graduate students: 20.5 Units
 
If you wish to enroll in more units than the maximum, you must seek approval from your college or school dean’s office (declared majors in Letters and Science should go to their department for approval). Requests are reviewed by the college after the adjustment period.
 

 
***Additional Registration Resources***
 
- [[Cancellation & Withdrawal - Office of the Registrar|Cancellation & Withdrawal]] 
- [[Visitor and Exchange Programs - Office of the Registrar|Visitor and Exchange Programs]] 
- [[Readmission - Office of the Registrar|Readmission]] 
- [[Suggested Classes - Office of the Registrar|Suggested Classes]] 
- [Free digital access to books, articles, and videos for classes](https://www.lib.berkeley.edu/find/course-reserves) 
- [Registration Status Check Tool](https://regstatus.sait-west.berkeley.edu/) – To access the tool, log in to the [campus VPN](https://security.berkeley.edu/services/bsecure/bsecure-remote-access-vpn) and copy/paste the URL into your browser: regstatus.sait-west.berkeley.edu

# Support for Staying Enrolled - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/cancellation-withdrawal/support-for-staying-enrolled/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/cancellation-withdrawal/support-for-staying-enrolled/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.775Z

## Content

Facing challenges that make it hard to stay enrolled in classes? Know that we care about you and are here to help. To make an informed decision about what’s best for you and your future, explore the resources below and be sure to [reach out to your college advisor](http://guide.berkeley.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/).
 
Are you ready to enroll and just haven’t gotten to it yet? Read about the next steps you should take now on the [[How to Enroll in Classes - Office of the Registrar|How to Enroll in Classes]] page.
 
## Get Support for Your Well-being
 
- [Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/caps) provides mental health resources to you. Call CAPS at (510) 642-9494, or call the after-hours counseling line at (855) 817-5667. Counselors are available for [virtual counseling appointments](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/caps-telementalhealth.pdf) by phone or video. 
- [Recalibrate](https://recalibrate.berkeley.edu/) can connect you to wellness resources designed for the entire campus community. 
- [The Basic Needs Center](http://basicneeds.berkeley.edu/) provides essential resources that impact your health, belonging, persistence, and overall well-being. Book a virtual appointment with the Basic Needs Manager by emailing basicneedssupport@berkeley.edu, or for immediate support call (510) 519-4003 (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
 
## Get financial support
 
- UC Berkeley has several resources to help if you’re struggling with financial concerns. For those struggling with unexpected expenses, you could be eligible for a [short-term emergency loan](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/types-of-aid-at-berkeley/loans/short-term-emergency-loan/), or it could make sense for you to apply for an [Economic Hardship Appeal](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/how-aid-works/appeals-special-circumstances/family-contribution-appeal/). 
- [Cal Student Central](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/) provides online and phone advising for financial aid, registration, and billing inquiries. Visit their website to access their [services and support](https://studentcentral.berkeley.edu/services-areas-support/). 
- Remember, remaining continuously enrolled can help you earn your degree on time and save you money in the long run.
 
## Get community care
 
- [The Centers for Educational Equity and Excellence (CE3)](https://ce3.berkeley.edu/) offer a comprehensive array of counseling programs, supplemental aid, and scholarships to support [former foster youth](https://hope.berkeley.edu/), [veterans](https://veteran.berkeley.edu/), [student parents](https://studentparents.berkeley.edu/), [undocumented students](https://undocu.berkeley.edu/), and [transfer students](https://transfers.berkeley.edu/) of all ages and life experiences. They aim to ensure the most vulnerable students achieve their potential. 
- Student parents can explore the Early [Childhood Education Program](https://ece.berkeley.edu/) and [UC Berkeley Youth Recreation](https://recwell.berkeley.edu/youth-recreation/). 
- [The Disabled Students’ Program](https://dsp.berkeley.edu/) provides you with accommodations and [services for disabilities](https://dsp.berkeley.edu/support-services/trio-dsp-student-support-services) in the academic environment. 
- [Community-specific health information](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/community-specific-information-and-services) and services offer a place where you can feel safe while still feeling connected to the Berkeley family. 
- The [Student Learning Center](https://slc.berkeley.edu/home) offers virtual services in many disciplines. 
- If you need hardware (e.g., laptop, noise-canceling headphones, webcam), you can apply for [STEP (Student Technology Equity Program)](https://technology.berkeley.edu/STEP). 
- The Berkeley International Office offers [services for International Students](https://internationaloffice.berkeley.edu/students/student-services).
 
## Helpful facts to know:
 
- You can explore the [Suggested Classes X feed](https://x.com/BerkeleyGuide) for classes with available seats. 
- **Insurance:** [SHIP insurance](https://uhs.berkeley.edu/insurance/ship-fees-enrollment) is dependent on enrollment. Make sure to check the end date of your insurance if you do not plan to stay enrolled. 
- **Loan Repayment:** If you are not enrolled for a period of 6 months, you could enter loan repayment. Read more at the [Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/manage-loans/repayment) website. 
- **Work-Study:** Enrollment can affect your UC Berkeley job. Students [can’t continue to earn work-study pay if they’re no longer enrolled](https://financialaid.berkeley.edu/work-study-frequently-asked-questions), which can affect their employer’s ability to retain them. Student staff positions also require you to be enrolled and typically only offer a limited grace period. Contact your employer to see how enrollment can affect your position.

# Transfer Credit - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/transfer-credit/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/transfer-credit/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.777Z

## Content

## Requirements for Transfer Credit
 
Check with your college or department to ensure you may use transfer coursework to complete a degree requirement. Once you have confirmed use of transfer credit, [review the criteria](https://ceu.berkeley.edu/transfer-credit/course-evaluation/) for eligibility from another college or university.
 
## Submitting Your Transcript
 
Follow these [submitting a transcript guidelines](https://ceu.berkeley.edu/transfer-credit/submit-and-review-transcripts/#submit) for how to submit your official transcript. For more information on the posting of transfer credit for newly admitted, continuing, and graduating students, review the [submit and review transcripts](https://ceu.berkeley.edu/transfer-credit/submit-and-review-transcripts/) page.
 
After the transcript is received and scanned, the evaluation of transfer credit for continuing students will take two to four weeks (one to two business days for graduating students) and will be posted to the Berkeley transcript. For more information, please visit the [Central Evaluation Unit](https://ceu.berkeley.edu/) website.
 
## Undergraduate Applicant Credit Transfer Questions
 
If you are a prospective undergraduate applicant with questions regarding enrollment in courses in preparation for applying to UC Berkeley as a transfer student, please visit the [Office of Undergraduate Admissions Transfer Requirements](https://admissions.berkeley.edu/transfer-requirements).
 
### Transferring Credit as a Graduate Student
 
If you are a graduate student, you can learn more about transferring credit through the [Graduate Division Admissions Requirements](http://grad.berkeley.edu/admissions/requirements/).
 
## Transfer Credit with the Central Evaluation Unit (CEU)
 
The Central Evaluation Unit (CEU) is responsible for reviewing and posting transfer credits for UC Berkeley undergraduates. Be sure to visit the [Central Evaluation Unit](https://ceu.berkeley.edu/) website for comprehensive information on:
 
- Enrolling in transfer courses and transferring credit. 
- Reviewing exam results, transfer credit, and academic progress reports. 
- Tracking completion of undergraduate degree requirements.
 
Information on how and when to contact the CEU is also included on the website.

## Content

[Academic Calendar](https://acadcalendar.com/category/academic-calendar/)  
# UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2026-2027: Important Dates
    **June 18, 2025   By [eriq elikplim](https://acadcalendar.com/author/eriq/)    ![UC Berkeley Academic Calendar.](https://acadcalendar.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/UC-Berkeley-Academic-Calendar-696x583.jpg)     
Share
    [**Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Facadcalendar.com%2Fuc-berkeley-academic-calendar%2F)[**X](https://x.com/intent/post?text=UC+Berkeley+Academic+Calendar+2026-2027%3A+Important+Dates&url=https%3A%2F%2Facadcalendar.com%2Fuc-berkeley-academic-calendar%2F&via=AcadCalendar)[**Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://acadcalendar.com/uc-berkeley-academic-calendar/&media=https://acadcalendar.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/UC-Berkeley-Academic-Calendar.jpg&description=UC+Berkeley+Academic+Calendar+2026-2027%3A+Important+Dates)[**WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=UC+Berkeley+Academic+Calendar+2026-2027%3A+Important+Dates%20%0A%0A%20https://acadcalendar.com/uc-berkeley-academic-calendar/)[**Telegram](https://telegram.me/share/url?url=https://acadcalendar.com/uc-berkeley-academic-calendar/&text=UC+Berkeley+Academic+Calendar+2026-2027%3A+Important+Dates)

[[UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2026-2027 Important Dates|**]]      
The UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2026-2027 covers all the essential dates, deadlines, and important information.
 
Whether you’re a new student, a continuing undergraduate, or a graduate student, stay organized with these crucial dates for the fall 2026, spring 2027, and summer 2026 semesters.
 
The University of California, Berkeley has two main semesters per academic year (Fall and Spring), plus optional summer sessions. This is different from the quarter systems used by some other universities.
 
Each semester runs approximately 15-16 weeks, allowing for more comprehensive coverage of course material.
 
## Table of Contents
 
## UC Berkeley Academic Calendar Fall 2026
 
- Fall 2026 Phase 1 continuing students enrollment ends on Friday, June 12, 2026. 
- Phase 1 new undergraduate transfer student enrollment begins on Tuesday, July 14, 2026. 
- Phase 1 new undergraduate freshman student enrollment begins on Thursday, July 16, 2026. 
- Phase 1 new graduate student enrollment begins on Friday, July 17, 2026. 
- Phase 2 continuing enrollment begins on Monday, July 20, 2026. 
- UC Berkeley Fall 2026 registration fees will be assessed tentatively on Monday, July 27, 2026. 
- Phase 1 new student enrollment ends on Sunday, August 16, 2026. 
- Phase 2 enrollment ends on Sunday, August 16, 2026. 
- Adjustment period begins on Monday, August 17, 2026. 
- UC Berkeley Fall 2026 Semester begins on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. 
- The fee payment deadline, either in full or the first installment under the Fee Payment Plan, is Friday, August 21, 2026. 
- The last day to withdraw for a full refund before instruction begins is Tuesday, August 25, 2026. 
- UC Berkeley Fall 2026 classes start on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, which is the first day of instruction. 
- The last day to drop classes without a fee is Friday, September 4, 2026. 
- The last day to drop Early Drop Deadline (EDD) courses is Friday, September 4, 2026. 
- **[Labor Day holiday](https://acadcalendar.com/labor-day-holiday-for-universities/)** will be observed on Monday, September 7, 2026. 
- The deadline to become officially registered by enrolling and paying at least 20% of tuition and fees is Friday, September 11, 2026. 
- The instructor drop deadline is Friday, September 11, 2026. 
- The last day to add classes without a fee is Friday, September 11, 2026. 
- The last day for undergraduates to add or drop classes and change units via the Enrollment Center is Wednesday, September 16, 2026. 
- The departmental schedulers and enrollment managers add, drop, swap, and unit change deadline is Friday, September 18, 2026. 
- UC Berkeley Homecoming Weekend 2026 will take place from Friday, October 9, through Saturday, October 10, 2026. 
- The adjustment period ends on Friday, October 30, 2026. 
- The department scheduler and enrollment managers grading option deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026. 
- The undergraduate and graduate students grading option deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026. 
- **[Veterans Day holiday](https://acadcalendar.com/veterans-day/)** will be observed on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. 
- UC Berkeley Thanksgiving Break 2026 will be observed on Wednesday, November 25, and Friday, November 27, 2026. 
- Formal classes for Fall 2026 semester end on Friday, December 4, 2026. 
- Reading, review, and recitation week or Fall 2026 RRR Week will take place from Monday, December 7, through Friday, December 11, 2026. 
- The last day of instruction is Friday, December 11, 2026. 
- The GSAOs and college advisers add, drop, swap, grading option, and unit change deadline is Friday, December 11, 2026. 
- Final examinations will be held from Monday, December 14, through Friday, December 18, 2026. 
- The Fall Semester ends on Friday, December 18, 2026. 
- Academic and administrative holidays will be observed on Thursday, December 24, and Friday, December 25, 2026, and on Thursday, December 31, 2026, and Friday, January 1, 2027. 
- Winter commencement will be held on a date to be determined.
 
## UC Berkeley Academic Calendar Spring 2027
 
- The Spring Semester begins on Tuesday, January 12, 2027. 
- **[MLK holiday](https://acadcalendar.com/martin-luther-king-jr-day/)** will be observed on Monday, January 18, 2027. 
- UC Berkeley Spring 2027 classes begins on Tuesday, January 19, 2027. 
- **[Presidents Day Holiday](https://acadcalendar.com/presidents-day/)** will be observed on Monday, February 15, 2027. 
- UC Berkeley Spring Break 2027 will take place from Monday, March 22, through Thursday, March 25, 2027. **[Cesar Chavez Day holiday](https://acadcalendar.com/cesar-chavez-day/)**will be observed on Friday, March 26, 2027. 
- Cal Day will be held on a date to be determined. 
- Formal classes end on Friday, April 30, 2027. 
- Reading, review, and recitation week will take place from Monday, May 3, through Friday, May 7, 2027. 
- The last day of instruction is Friday, May 7, 2027. 
- Final examinations will be held from Monday, May 10, through Friday, May 14, 2027. 
- The Spring Semester ends on Friday, May 14, 2027. 
- Commencement will take place on Saturday, May 15, 2027.
 
## UC Berkeley Academic Calendar Summer 2026
 
- Session A (Six Weeks) begins on Tuesday, May 26, 2026. 
- Session B (Ten Weeks) begins on Monday, June 8, 2026. 
- Session C (Eight Weeks) begins on Monday, June 22, 2026. 
- Session A ends on Thursday, July 2, 2026. 
- Session D (Six Weeks) begins on Monday, July 6, 2026. 
- Session F (Three Weeks) begins on Monday, July 6, 2026. 
- Session F ends on Friday, July 24, 2026, according to the UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2025-2026. 
- Session E (Three Weeks) begins on Monday, July 27, 2026. 
- Sessions B, C, D, and E end on Friday, August 14, 2026.
 
## UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2026-2027 FAQs
    
### What day does UC Berkeley start in fall 2026?
  
UC Berkeley Fall 2026 semester officially begins on **Wednesday, August 19, 2026**, with classes starting on **Wednesday, August 26, 2026**
    
### When does Fall 2026 enrollment begin at UC Berkeley?
  
New undergraduate transfer students can begin enrolling on July 14, 2026, followed by freshmen on July 17, and graduate students on July 17. Continuing students start Phase 2 enrollment on July 20, 2026.
    
### When does the Spring 2027 semester start at UC Berkeley?
  
The Spring 2027 semester begins on Tuesday, January 12, 2027, with instruction starting on January 19, 2027. Final exams run from May 10-14, 2027, and commencement is scheduled for Saturday, May 15, 2027.
    
### What is Cal Day at UC Berkeley?
  
Cal Day is UC Berkeley’s annual open house event for newly admitted students and families.
 
The program begins with a Welcome Session at California Memorial Stadium at 9 a.m. Afterwards, students visit their academic departments, learn about resources and opportunities for Berkeley students, take a campus tour, and much more. The 2026 Cal Day date is To Be Determined (check [calday.berkeley.edu](https://admit.berkeley.edu/calday/) for updates).
    
### Can I take a semester off from UC Berkeley?
  
Yes, UC Berkeley allows students to take a leave of absence. Contact the Registrar’s Office for specific procedures and deadlines for your situation.
    
### What is RRR Week at UC Berkeley?
  
RRR Week (Reading/Review/Recitation Week) is a dedicated academic period at UC Berkeley held the week **after formal classes end**and **before final exams**.
 
Functionally similar to “reading day(s)” at other universities, it provides students with uninterrupted time to synthesize course material, prepare for finals, and complete projects without new assignments or lectures. Rooted in the University of California, Berkeley’s academic traditions, it emphasizes three pillars:
 
**Reading**: Self-directed study.
**Review:** Consolidating course content.
**Recitation:** Peer-led collaborative sessions.
    
### How is RRR Week different from the previous “Dead Days” or “Dead Week”?
  
Historically, “dead days” referred to the two informal days between the end of classes and exams, while “dead week” (15th week of the semester) followed [recommendations dating to 1954](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/07192024_Campus-Policies-and-Guidelines-Concerning-the-Academic-Calendar.pdf) that prohibited introducing new material to allow student review.
 
However, these periods lacked structured academic engagement.
 
RRR Week, introduced as a formal instructional period, expands this concept:
 
**Extended Time**: Replaces the shorter “dead days” with a full week for preparation.
 
**Active Engagement**: Instructors are expected to hold office hours, offer consultations, or host optional reviews/feedback sessions, unlike the passive nature of “dead week.”
 
**Instructional Recognition**: Though formal classes do not meet, RRR Week is counted as part of the academic term, emphasizing its role in the learning process.
This shift reflects UC Berkeley’s focus on fostering intentional, supported academic preparation ahead of exams.
     
For more on the UC Berkeley Academic Calendar 2026-2027, visit the [University of California, Berkeley Registrar website](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/calendars/academic-calendar/).

# Undergraduate Classifications - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/how-to-enroll-in-classes/undergraduate-classifications/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/enrollment/how-to-enroll-in-classes/undergraduate-classifications/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.775Z

## Content

As a UC Berkeley undergraduate student, you have two classifications: academic level and terms in attendance.
 
**Academic Level**
 
Academic Level is based upon your total earned units. Note: transfer students may have an inaccurate academic level until both the semester begins and their transfer credit is processed.
 
- Freshman | fewer than 30 units 
- Sophomore | 30 to 59 units 
- Junior | 60 to 89 units 
- Senior | 90 or more units
 
**Terms in Attendance**
 
Terms in attendance are based on the number of terms you have been attending Berkeley. If you entered Berkeley as a transfer student your terms in attendance start at 5. Only fall and spring terms are counted. Summer terms are excluded. Terms in attendance designations:
 
- 1 – first-year admits 
- 2 
- 3 
- 4 
- 5 – transfer students 
- 6 
- 7 – senior year 
- 8 
- 8+
 
## Maintain Your Course Loads
 
To ensure your academic level remains on par with your terms in attendance, you are required to maintain a normal course load.
 
**Normal Course Loads**
 
- Undergraduate students: A course load of 15 units per semester is considered a normal undergraduate course load. You are generally expected to enroll in at least 15 units. Some colleges have a minimum course load requirement of 12 or 13 units. 
- Graduate students: A course load of 12 units per semester is considered a normal, full-time graduate course load.
 
**Reduced Course Loads for Undergraduates**
 
Reduced course loads must be approved by the dean’s office of your college or school. If you are an undergraduate and anticipate being enrolled in fewer than the minimum number of units required by your college or school, contact your dean’s office as soon as possible to request approval to be enrolled in a less-than-full course load. Requests should be submitted before the end of the previous semester to have time for review. A reduced course load must be approved by the dean of your college or school before the end of your Phase II enrollment period.

# Update Name & Personal Information - Office of the Registrar

- **Source URL**: [https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/update-name-personal-information/](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/academic-records/update-name-personal-information/)
- **Crawled At**: 2026-07-15T07:10:08.778Z

## Content

There are multiple options for displaying your name and personal information on records, rosters, and other university systems. Students can update the following details in CalCentral:
 
- Provide their lived name (a self-chosen personal and/or preferred professional first, middle, and last name used instead of a legal name). 
- Select which name (lived or legal) they want each delegate to see. 
- Indicate their gender identity, sexual orientation, and pronouns.
 
**Display Name in the Campus Directory**
 
Students have the option to select how personal data is displayed in the directory by using a drop-down menu for each field. Display options include:
 
- Public (everyone can see this field; this is the default setting) 
- Logged in (only those logged in via CalNet can see this field) 
- Not visible (no one can see this field)
 
Please note: If a student does not identify their lived name, the name field will default to the legal name. Once you make these updates in CalCentral, the information will be synced across multiple university systems, and you will see it reflected in your directory listing, bCourses, Google Workspace (bConnected, bCal, bMail, bDrive), and more.
 
## How to Update Name & Personal Information
       
- Unless you have identified your lived name, the name field will default to your legal name. To view your name data or change your lived name, follow these steps:
 
- Log in to [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/dashboard). 
- Click your Avatar (in the top right corner). 
- From the dropdown menu, select Personal Profile to review how your name is displayed. 
- To update lived name: Starting from the Personal Profile tab, click on the lived name value. Make edits to your first, middle, and/or last name, then click save. You cannot use special (non-ASCII) characters in your lived name.
 
For information about how your name appears on your diploma, visit the [[Diplomas - Office of the Registrar|Diplomas]] page. If you need to update your **legal name**, follow the directions below for how do I change (or correct) my legal name?
- If you have access to [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/), you may change your legal name on university records by submitting a Legal Name Change Petition eForm. We have step-by-step instructions for how to petition [legal name change as a current student (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/Legal-Name-Change-Petition-Active-Students_a11y.pdf) and [legal name change as an alumni (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/Legal-Name-Change-Petition-Alumni-Portal_a11y.pdf). The turnaround time for changes to your name is up to 5 business days from when your paperwork is received by our office.
 
If you are an alumni without access to CalCentral, see the directions below for how to change (or correct) my legal name without CalCentral access.
- - Alumni who graduated in Fall 2016 and later can complete this [form to change their lived name or request a change of legal name](http://bcsweb.is.berkeley.edu/psc/extern/GUEST/FORM/c/UC_SS_G3FRAME.UC_SS_G3SEARCH_FL.GBL?G3FORM_TASK=ADD&G3FORM_TYPE=SRNAME&G3FORM_CONDITION=Default). Note: The linked form may take a few moments to authenticate and load. 
- Alumni who graduated before Fall 2016 must mail in a completed [Petition for Change of Name after Awarding Degree (PDF)](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/NameChangeDeg.pdf) along with proper documentation.
- Missing SSN/ITIN Information
 
- To add your SSN/ITIN, follow these steps: 
- Log in to [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/dashboard). 
- Click your Avatar (in the top-right corner). 
- From the drop-down, select Personal Profile. 
- In Personal Details, click on Add SSN/Add ITIN. 
- A pop-up window will appear, carefully enter your SSN/ITIN without any hyphens or spaces. Once information is saved, you will not be able to make additional edits through CalCentral. 
- Click Add to save.
 
Incorrect SSN/ITIN Information or Inactive Student Status
 
- If your SSN/ITIN is incorrect on CalCentral or if you are no longer an active student with UC Berkeley, please complete and submit this [form](https://registrar.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/SSN_Request_a11y.pdf) (see form for submission instructions).
- To view and update your biographical data, including your gender identity, sexual orientation, and pronouns, follow these steps:
 
- Log in to [CalCentral](https://calcentral.berkeley.edu/dashboard). 
- Click your Avatar (in the top right corner). 
- From the dropdown menu, select Personal Profile. 
- Click the Biographic tab. The Gender Identity and Sexual Orientation fields are initially populated with information provided on your university admission application. You can update these at any time.
 
Selecting pronouns is highly recommended. You can add and update your pronouns at any time. Once selected, they will be displayed below your name on:
 
- CalCentral > My Academics > Academic Profile 
- CalCentral > My Academics > Semesters card > View Academic Summary
 
Review the information icons (“i” icons) in CalCentral to learn more.
- Add and manage your delegates under CalCentral > Avatar > Personal Profile > Delegate Access.
 
- Any delegate you added prior to Oct. 8, 2023, will default to displaying your legal name, but you can update the name that displays to your delegates at any time. 
- Any delegate you add on or after Oct. 8, 2023, will include the selection of either the legal or lived name to display to the delegate.
 
Regardless of the choices above, delegates will see your legal name in the payment system accessed via CalCentral > My Finances > Billing Summary > Make Payment button or View PDF Statement link.
- First and last name values are required in CalCentral. Enter a period “.” in the first name field and enter your mononym in the last name field.
- For students who have a dual role as students and staff, CalCentral is the primary location for updating their name and biographic data. However, for employee-related updates such as benefits selections or direct deposit information, please log in to the [UCPath](https://ucpath.universityofcalifornia.edu/saml_login) system.
